name: CI

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
      - name: Prepare Rust toolchain
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --component rustfmt,clippy
          rustup default stable
      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Frontend lint
        run: npm run lint
      - name: Release metadata
        run: npm run check:release-metadata
      - name: Frontend tests
        run: npm test
      - name: Frontend production build
        run: npm run build
      - name: Rust format
        run: cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --check
      - name: Rust clippy
        run: cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: Rust tests
        run: cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml

```powershell
npm ci
npm run tauri dev
```

Run project checks:

```powershell
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run test
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml
cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Build the Windows installer and checksum file:

```powershell
npm run release:windows
```

## Browser Chat Extension

A Chromium browser extension (Chrome, Edge, and other Chromium-based browsers) manages ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok and DeepSeek web conversations independently of the desktop app: organize, search, export, and delete them, with data kept on the local machine only. See the [extension guide](extension/README.md) for installation and usage.

## Project Documentation

- [Session data behavior and safety boundaries](docs/sessions.md)
- [API service (local gateway)](docs/gateway.md)
- [Development, verification, cleanup, and maintainer handoff](docs/development.md)

repository.readme: # Emend [![CI](https://github.com/chliu1990/obsidian-emend/actions/workflows/ci.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/chliu1990/obsidian-emend/actions/workflows/ci.yaml) Emend is a desktop Obsidian plugin for streaming AI chat and safe, reviewable edits to your Markdown notes. It supports DeepSeek, Kimi Code, and custom OpenAI-compatible providers, with **Track Changes** as the review surface for every AI edit. ## Features - **Chat with context:** Ask questions, discuss ideas, or brainstorm with the active note. Responses and reasoning stream into the sidebar; these modes never write to your notes. - **Research on the web explicitly:** For DeepSeek `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`, the read-only composer offers **Web: Off** (the default), **Review**, and **Auto**. The model can direct sequential search/fetch calls across multiple rounds; Review shows editable call batches, and actual retrieved HTTP(S) results become stable, safe citations. Search returns bounded page content before Fetch is needed. Expected Fetch failures become visible unread-page outcomes instead of failing the whole answer, while credential/account errors remain fatal. Folded Web activity preserves query/URL/status metadata locally. Web retrieval never writes notes. Kimi/custom providers and other models are unsupported, with no silent unsearched fallback. - **Add notes explicitly:** Use **Add notes** in chat or Modify Selection to include bounded, read-only snapshots of other Markdown notes. Paths stay visible with remove/clear controls; selections belong to the active target note, last only for the current plugin session, and clear when the Emend plugin or Obsidian reloads. - **Edit with confidence:** Full-note and selection edits use a closed Operations protocol—`insert`, `remove`, `replace`, and `comment`—with exact anchors and atomic validation before anything is written. - **Target selections directly:** Select text and focus chat to default **Edit target** to **Selection**, then use a typed Edit request or any quick action. Choose **Full note** explicitly when needed. Selection edits use native Obsidian undo and show concise chat results with reasoning and token usage. - **Review every change:** Valid operations become CriticMarkup that you can accept or reject in Track Changes. Emend has no competing diff or Apply button. - **Work quickly:** Use **Fix grammar**, **Make concise**, or **Add examples** in chat or the selection modal, with keyboard shortcuts and native undo. - **Keep your place:** Per-note conversations persist locally, multi-turn edits retain earlier review markup, and note/source changes invalidate stale responses. - **Stay in control:** Include optional `AGENTS.md` instructions and skills, configure context limits, and see provider-reported or clearly labelled estimated token usage. ## Requirements - Desktop Obsidian **1.11.4 or newer**; mobile is not supported. - **Track Changes**, installed and enabled separately for edit review. - A DeepSeek, Kimi Code, or custom OpenAI-compatible provider with an available model and API key. Emend does not install other plugins automatically. ## Installation Emend is distributed through GitHub releases and manual installation. An Obsidian Community Directory submission is not currently planned; see [publication and distribution](devel_docs/publication.md). See the complete [installation guide](INSTALLATION.md) for build, update, removal, and troubleshooting instructions. **Recommended: install with BRAT.** Install and enable **BRAT — Beta Reviewers Auto-update Tool** from Obsidian’s community plugins, choose **Add beta plugin** in BRAT, and enter `https://github.com/chliu1990/obsidian-emend`. BRAT installs Emend from GitHub releases and can keep it updated. Enable **Emend** and **Track Changes** after installation. See the [BRAT installation tutorial](INSTALLATION.md#install-with-brat). Alternatively, download `emend-2.7.0.zip` from the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/chliu1990/obsidian-emend/releases) and extract it into `/.obsidian/plugins/`. The ZIP contains the complete `emend/` plugin folder. For a source installation, clone this repository and run: ```bash npm ci npm run build ``` Then copy `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css` into: ```text /.obsidian/plugins/emend/ ``` Open **Settings → Community plugins**, reload plugins, and enable **Emend** and **Track Changes**. ## Quick start 1. Open **Settings → Emend** and configure a provider: | Provider | Base URL | Default model | | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `deepseek-flash` | | Kimi Code | `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1` | `k3.1-pro` | | Custom | Your OpenAI-compatible base URL | Your model | Emend appends `/chat/completions` to the base URL. Models and URLs remain editable. To populate the model selector, click the compact **Refresh models** icon in **Settings → Emend**. This explicitly sends an authenticated `GET /models` request using the provider's API key from SecretStorage; discovery never runs automatically. Returned model IDs and display names become dropdown options, while the current selection and editable custom-model entry remain available. Discovered lists persist locally, and changing a provider's base URL or API key clears only that provider's list. Custom endpoints that do not support `/models`, HTTP failures, and malformed responses show an error without replacing the previous list. 2. Open **Emend chat** from the ribbon or Command Palette. 3. Select **Ask**, **Discuss**, or **Brainstorm** and submit a question. The note stays unchanged. 4. Optionally use the composer **Web** control with DeepSeek `deepseek-flash` or `deepseek-v4-pro`. **Off** is the default; **Review** shows each model-proposed search/fetch batch with editable queries/URLs, while **Auto** runs validated batches directly. The model may use multiple rounds and sequential calls up to **Settings → Emend → Web tool call limit** (default 8, range 1–20). Retrieved content shares a 40,000-character submission budget, with at most 12,000 characters per fetched page. The disclosure warns that arguments may contain note-derived text and successful DeepSeek retrieval may be billed separately. Web is unavailable in Edit and for Kimi/custom providers or unsupported models; failures never silently become unsearched answers. 5. Optionally click **Add notes** to choose other Markdown notes as read-only context for the next request. Review their visible paths and use **Remove** or **Clear all** as needed; these per-target selections survive note switches during the current plugin session and clear when the Emend plugin or Obsidian reloads. 6. For a full-note change, choose **Edit target: Full note**, then select **Edit** or a quick action. Review the resulting markup in Track Changes. 7. For a smaller edit, select text and focus chat. **Edit target** defaults to **Selection**; enter an Edit instruction or use **Fix grammar**, **Make concise**, or **Add examples**. Only the captured range changes, native undo restores it, and chat shows a concise result with reasoning and token usage. If the selection is empty, whitespace-only, or vanishes before submission, Emend fails closed without requesting or writing instead of falling back to Full note. 8. Alternatively, run **Modify selected text with AI** from the Command Palette. The unchanged modal accepts an instruction or quick action and shares the same target note's additional-note selections, but does not add a chat result or usage/retry display. Follow the guided [quick start](QUICK_START.md) for detailed verification steps, skills, shortcuts, and operation-based editing examples. ## Header shortcuts and build identity The chat header lists Emend's visible default shortcuts: | Action | macOS | Windows/Linux | | --- | --- | --- | | Ask mode | `⌘⇧A Ask` | `Ctrl+Shift+A Ask` | | Edit mode | `⌘⇧E Edit` | `Ctrl+Shift+E Edit` | | Send | `Enter / ⌘ Enter send` | `Enter / Ctrl+Enter send` | | Newline | `Shift Enter newline` | `Shift+Enter newline` | These labels describe the defaults; they do not change when you remap hotkeys in Obsidian. The **Open Emend chat** command has no default hotkey. The compact identity beside the **Emend** title shows the manifest version in release builds. Development and other untagged builds show the short Git commit hash instead. Development watch mode captures that hash when it starts, so restart `npm run dev` after a commit to update the displayed identity. ## Safe editing model Emend never lets the model rewrite a document directly. It returns a bare JSON array of closed operations against the captured source. Emend then: 1. Requires exact anchors and unique matches or explicit one-based occurrences, with typed diagnostics that identify the operation, failure code, and bounded match details. 2. Rejects malformed, ambiguous, overlapping, or markup-injecting commands. Declared-range overlap and insertion-ambiguity rules remain conservative even when smaller review hunks could otherwise coexist. 3. Rejects partial inline-code targets (`inline-code-range`), fenced-code edits (`fenced-code-edit`), and table structure changes (`table-structure-edit`) atomically. Tables allow text edits within one existing header/body cell, including safe insert/remove/replace/comment Operations and escaped pipes. Selection uses full-note context only for structural classification, never target expansion. 4. Compiles valid operations into CriticMarkup and revalidates the result. Broad replacements are reduced to deterministic Unicode word/segment-level hunks—not character-minimal fragments—with whole-target fallback for backtick-containing replacements and a bounded single-substitution fallback for expensive responses. 5. If candidate validation fails, automatically makes one correction request to the same provider (at most two provider calls total). The unchanged original request is resubmitted with the invalid response and bounded diagnostic feedback; there is no delay, backoff, or new retry setting. A second invalid response is terminal. 6. Checks that the captured file and source have not changed and that the request was not aborted, then writes once so Track Changes can review the edit. Provider failures, aborts, stale targets, and write failures are terminal rather than triggers for another correction round. Full-note Edit always sends the complete note. Composer Selection and Modify Selection send the complete selection plus surrounding context with empty provider history, but replace only the captured range through native `editor.replaceRange`. Both selection entry points use the same minimization and validation-correction flow. Composer full-note and Selection results include all attempted rounds' token usage and retain only successful-attempt reasoning after correction. The separate selection modal keeps its existing notices without a usage footer or retry-status display. Raw operations, invalid responses, and correction feedback remain transient rather than ready-chat content or persisted history. Model history retains each ready message's mode, historical note-write permission, and origin. Local Edit confirmations are labeled as local outcomes, not model responses. These annotations describe earlier requests only: the currently selected mode alone controls note-write access, so an earlier Edit never grants writing to a later Ask, Discuss, or Brainstorm request. ## Privacy and local data Emend makes **no background AI requests**. Content is sent only when you explicitly submit a chat or edit action. - Note context, prompts, recent ready history, explicitly selected additional-note snapshots, and any loaded `AGENTS.md`/skill instructions are sent to the selected provider as required for that request. Picking, opening, or switching notes sends nothing and does not read additional-note content. - With **Web: Review** or **Auto**, those ordinary model-round contents go to DeepSeek, which may derive search queries and fetch URLs from them. DeepSeek search/fetch endpoints receive only the visible validated arguments; Review permits editing every proposed batch. Retrieved text is untrusted external data and never writes notes or becomes instructions/skills. Successful retrieval may be billed separately. Changing the Web control, opening a note, loading a thread, or rendering citations performs no retrieval. - Full-note Edit sends the entire active note. Read-only chat uses bounded active-note context. Composer Selection and Modify Selection send the complete selection and bounded surrounding context with empty provider history; they never truncate the selection to fit the context budget. Additional notes use a separate combined source-character budget and are read-only in every mode. Web search is unavailable to Edit, quick actions, and Modify Selection. An invalid edit candidate can cause one automatic second call to the same provider, containing the unchanged original request plus that candidate and bounded validation feedback; this possible extra call has no separate setting and may incur provider charges. - Note and vault paths are sent only when **Include note path** is enabled. With it off, additional-note sections have generic numbered labels without their paths; with it on, they include vault-qualified paths. The local controls always show selected paths before submission. - API keys are stored in **Obsidian SecretStorage**, not plaintext `data.json`. Legacy plaintext keys are migrated automatically. - Ready conversations are stored locally under `/.obsidian/emend/chats/` using schema 2; version 1 threads load and become schema 2 on the next save. Ready Review/Auto badges, sanitized result-backed citations, and folded Web activity (search queries, fetch URLs, and completed/failed/skipped outcomes) may persist. API keys, raw request bodies/tool arguments/results, retrieved content, transient activity, additional-note selections/snapshots, loading/error/stopped states, and buffered edit responses are not persisted. - Deleting a note does not automatically delete its saved conversation. See the [privacy and storage details](QUICK_START.md#8-verify-persistence-and-privacy-behavior) and [installation/removal guide](INSTALLATION.md#remove-emend) for cleanup instructions. ## Documentation - [Installation guide](INSTALLATION.md) - [Quick start](QUICK_START.md) - [Architecture and implementation records](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) - [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) and [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) - [DeepSeek online search implementation](devel_docs/36-deepseek-online-search.md) - [Minimal edit ranges and guarded correction](devel_docs/37-minimal-edit-ranges.md) - [Markdown edit safeguards and verification](devel_docs/38-markdown-edit-safeguards.md) - [Easier selected-text editing and verification](devel_docs/39-easier-selection-editing.md) - [Contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [security policy](SECURITY.md) - [CI and release workflows](.github/workflows/) - [Deferred context-management roadmap](devel_docs/future-context-management.md) - [Remaining web-search roadmap](devel_docs/future-web-search.md) - [Provider and context feature backlog](devel_docs/future-provider-and-context-features.md) Deferred documents describe possible future work, not features in this release; the web-search roadmap separately identifies the implemented DeepSeek baseline. ## Development ```bash npm ci npm test npm run lint npm run build ``` Emend uses TypeScript, strict checks, Vitest, and esbuild. The plugin is desktop-only because its provider transport uses browser `fetch` with Server-Sent Events. ## Attribution Emend is based on Lapis Lazuli AI Assistant by Taha Yiğit Melek. See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md) and the MIT [LICENSE](LICENSE) for attribution. Maintained by **Chang Liu and Kimi K3.1 Pro**. This project was driven by vibecoding with **Kimi K3.1 Pro** using **Kimi Code**.

The model can direct sequential search/fetch calls across multiple rounds; Review shows editable call batches, and actual retrieved HTTP(S) results become stable, safe citations. Search returns bounded page content before Fetch is needed. Expected Fetch failures become visible unread-page outcomes instead of failing the whole answer, while credential/account errors remain fatal. Folded Web activity preserves query/URL/status metadata locally. Web retrieval never writes notes. Kimi/custom providers and other models are unsupported, with no silent unsearched fallback. - **Add notes explicitly:** Use **Add notes** in chat or Modify Selection to include bounded, read-only snapshots of other Markdown notes. Paths stay visible with remove/clear controls; selections belong to the active target note, last only for the current plugin session, and clear when the Emend plugin or Obsidian reloads. - **Edit with confidence:** Full-note and selection edits use a closed Operations protocol—`insert`, `remove`, `replace`, and `comment`—with exact anchors and atomic validation before anything is written. - **Target selections directly:** Select text and focus chat to default **Edit target** to **Selection**, then use a typed Edit request or any quick action. Choose **Full note** explicitly when needed. Selection edits use native Obsidian undo and show concise chat results with reasoning and token usage. - **Review every change:** Valid operations become CriticMarkup that you can accept or reject in Track Changes. Emend has no competing diff or Apply button. - **Work quickly:** Use **Fix grammar**, **Make concise**, or **Add examples** in chat or the selection modal, with keyboard shortcuts and native undo. - **Keep your place:** Per-note conversations persist locally, multi-turn edits retain earlier review markup, and note/source changes invalidate stale responses. - **Stay in control:** Include optional `AGENTS.md` instructions and skills, configure context limits, and see provider-reported or clearly labelled estimated token usage. ## Requirements - Desktop Obsidian **1.11.4 or newer**; mobile is not supported. - **Track Changes**, installed and enabled separately for edit review. - A DeepSeek, Kimi Code, or custom OpenAI-compatible provider with an available model and API key. Emend does not install other plugins automatically. ## Installation Emend is distributed through GitHub releases and manual installation. An Obsidian Community Directory submission is not currently planned; see [publication and distribution](devel_docs/publication.md). See the complete [installation guide](INSTALLATION.md) for build, update, removal, and troubleshooting instructions. **Recommended: install with BRAT.** Install and enable **BRAT — Beta Reviewers Auto-update Tool** from Obsidian’s community plugins, choose **Add beta plugin** in BRAT, and enter `https://github.com/chliu1990/obsidian-emend`. BRAT installs Emend from GitHub releases and can keep it updated. Enable **Emend** and **Track Changes** after installation. See the [BRAT installation tutorial](INSTALLATION.md#install-with-brat). Alternatively, download `emend-2.7.0.zip` from the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/chliu1990/obsidian-emend/releases) and extract it into `/.obsidian/plugins/`. The ZIP contains the complete `emend/` plugin folder. For a source installation, clone this repository and run: ```bash npm ci npm run build ``` Then copy `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css` into: ```text /.obsidian/plugins/emend/ ``` Open **Settings → Community plugins**, reload plugins, and enable **Emend** and **Track Changes**. ## Quick start 1. Open **Settings → Emend** and configure a provider: | Provider | Base URL | Default model | | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `deepseek-flash` | | Kimi Code | `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1` | `k3.1-pro` | | Custom | Your OpenAI-compatible base URL | Your model | Emend appends `/chat/completions` to the base URL. Models and URLs remain editable. To populate the model selector, click the compact **Refresh models** icon in **Settings → Emend**. This explicitly sends an authenticated `GET /models` request using the provider's API key from SecretStorage; discovery never runs automatically. Returned model IDs and display names become dropdown options, while the current selection and editable custom-model entry remain available. Discovered lists persist locally, and changing a provider's base URL or API key clears only that provider's list. Custom endpoints that do not support `/models`, HTTP failures, and malformed responses show an error without replacing the previous list. 2. Open **Emend chat** from the ribbon or Command Palette. 3. Select **Ask**, **Discuss**, or **Brainstorm** and submit a question. The note stays unchanged. 4. Optionally use the composer **Web** control with DeepSeek `deepseek-flash` or `deepseek-v4-pro`. **Off** is the default; **Review** shows each model-proposed search/fetch batch with editable queries/URLs, while **Auto** runs validated batches directly. The model may use multiple rounds and sequential calls up to **Settings → Emend → Web tool call limit** (default 8, range 1–20). Retrieved content shares a 40,000-character submission budget, with at most 12,000 characters per fetched page. The disclosure warns that arguments may contain note-derived text and successful DeepSeek retrieval may be billed separately. Web is unavailable in Edit and for Kimi/custom providers or unsupported models; failures never silently become unsearched answers. 5. Optionally click **Add notes** to choose other Markdown notes as read-only context for the next request. Review their visible paths and use **Remove** or **Clear all** as needed; these per-target selections survive note switches during the current plugin session and clear when the Emend plugin or Obsidian reloads. 6. For a full-note change, choose **Edit target: Full note**, then select **Edit** or a quick action. Review the resulting markup in Track Changes. 7. For a smaller edit, select text and focus chat. **Edit target** defaults to **Selection**; enter an Edit instruction or use **Fix grammar**, **Make concise**, or **Add examples**. Only the captured range changes, native undo restores it, and chat shows a concise result with reasoning and token usage. If the selection is empty, whitespace-only, or vanishes before submission, Emend fails closed without requesting or writing instead of falling back to Full note. 8. Alternatively, run **Modify selected text with AI** from the Command Palette. The unchanged modal accepts an instruction or quick action and shares the same target note's additional-note selections, but does not add a chat result or usage/retry display. Follow the guided [quick start](QUICK_START.md) for detailed verification steps, skills, shortcuts, and operation-based editing examples. ## Header shortcuts and build identity The chat header lists Emend's visible default shortcuts: | Action | macOS | Windows/Linux | | --- | --- | --- | | Ask mode | `⌘⇧A Ask` | `Ctrl+Shift+A Ask` | | Edit mode | `⌘⇧E Edit` | `Ctrl+Shift+E Edit` | | Send | `Enter / ⌘ Enter send` | `Enter / Ctrl+Enter send` | | Newline | `Shift Enter newline` | `Shift+Enter newline` | These labels describe the defaults; they do not change when you remap hotkeys in Obsidian. The **Open Emend chat** command has no default hotkey. The compact identity beside the **Emend** title shows the manifest version in release builds. Development and other untagged builds show the short Git commit hash instead. Development watch mode captures that hash when it starts, so restart `npm run dev` after a commit to update the displayed identity. ## Safe editing model Emend never lets the model rewrite a document directly. It returns a bare JSON array of closed operations against the captured source. Emend then: 1. Requires exact anchors and unique matches or explicit one-based occurrences, with typed diagnostics that identify the operation, failure code, and bounded match details. 2. Rejects malformed, ambiguous, overlapping, or markup-injecting commands. Declared-range overlap and insertion-ambiguity rules remain conservative even when smaller review hunks could otherwise coexist. 3. Rejects partial inline-code targets (`inline-code-range`), fenced-code edits (`fenced-code-edit`), and table structure changes (`table-structure-edit`) atomically. Tables allow text edits within one existing header/body cell, including safe insert/remove/replace/comment Operations and escaped pipes. Selection uses full-note context only for structural classification, never target expansion. 4. Compiles valid operations into CriticMarkup and revalidates the result. Broad replacements are reduced to deterministic Unicode word/segment-level hunks—not character-minimal fragments—with whole-target fallback for backtick-containing replacements and a bounded single-substitution fallback for expensive responses. 5. If candidate validation fails, automatically makes one correction request to the same provider (at most two provider calls total). The unchanged original request is resubmitted with the invalid response and bounded diagnostic feedback; there is no delay, backoff, or new retry setting. A second invalid response is terminal. 6. Checks that the captured file and source have not changed and that the request was not aborted, then writes once so Track Changes can review the edit. Provider failures, aborts, stale targets, and write failures are terminal rather than triggers for another correction round. Full-note Edit always sends the complete note. Composer Selection and Modify Selection send the complete selection plus surrounding context with empty provider history, but replace only the captured range through native `editor.replaceRange`. Both selection entry points use the same minimization and validation-correction flow. Composer full-note and Selection results include all attempted rounds' token usage and retain only successful-attempt reasoning after correction. The separate selection modal keeps its existing notices without a usage footer or retry-status display. Raw operations, invalid responses, and correction feedback remain transient rather than ready-chat content or persisted history. Model history retains each ready message's mode, historical note-write permission, and origin. Local Edit confirmations are labeled as local outcomes, not model responses. These annotations describe earlier requests only: the currently selected mode alone controls note-write access, so an earlier Edit never grants writing to a later Ask, Discuss, or Brainstorm request. ## Privacy and local data Emend makes **no background AI requests**. Content is sent only when you explicitly submit a chat or edit action. - Note context, prompts, recent ready history, explicitly selected additional-note snapshots, and any loaded `AGENTS.md`/skill instructions are sent to the selected provider as required for that request. Picking, opening, or switching notes sends nothing and does not read additional-note content. - With **Web: Review** or **Auto**, those ordinary model-round contents go to DeepSeek, which may derive search queries and fetch URLs from them. DeepSeek search/fetch endpoints receive only the visible validated arguments; Review permits editing every proposed batch. Retrieved text is untrusted external data and never writes notes or becomes instructions/skills. Successful retrieval may be billed separately. Changing the Web control, opening a note, loading a thread, or rendering citations performs no retrieval. - Full-note Edit sends the entire active note. Read-only chat uses bounded active-note context. Composer Selection and Modify Selection send the complete selection and bounded surrounding context with empty provider history; they never truncate the selection to fit the context budget. Additional notes use a separate combined source-character budget and are read-only in every mode. Web search is unavailable to Edit, quick actions, and Modify Selection. An invalid edit candidate can cause one automatic second call to the same provider, containing the unchanged original request plus that candidate and bounded validation feedback; this possible extra call has no separate setting and may incur provider charges. - Note and vault paths are sent only when **Include note path** is enabled. With it off, additional-note sections have generic numbered labels without their paths; with it on, they include vault-qualified paths. The local controls always show selected paths before submission. - API keys are stored in **Obsidian SecretStorage**, not plaintext `data.json`. Legacy plaintext keys are migrated automatically. - Ready conversations are stored locally under `/.obsidian/emend/chats/` using schema 2; version 1 threads load and become schema 2 on the next save. Ready Review/Auto badges, sanitized result-backed citations, and folded Web activity (search queries, fetch URLs, and completed/failed/skipped outcomes) may persist. API keys, raw request bodies/tool arguments/results, retrieved content, transient activity, additional-note selections/snapshots, loading/error/stopped states, and buffered edit responses are not persisted. - Deleting a note does not automatically delete its saved conversation. See the [privacy and storage details](QUICK_START.md#8-verify-persistence-and-privacy-behavior) and [installation/removal guide](INSTALLATION.md#remove-emend) for cleanup instructions. ## Documentation - [Installation guide](INSTALLATION.md) - [Quick start](QUICK_START.md) - [Architecture and implementation records](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) - [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) and [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) - [DeepSeek online search implementation](devel_docs/36-deepseek-online-search.md) - [Minimal edit ranges and guarded correction](devel_docs/37-minimal-edit-ranges.md) - [Markdown edit safeguards and verification](devel_docs/38-markdown-edit-safeguards.md) - [Easier selected-text editing and verification](devel_docs/39-easier-selection-editing.md) - [Contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [security policy](SECURITY.md) - [CI and release workflows](.github/workflows/) - [Deferred context-management roadmap](devel_docs/future-context-management.md) - [Remaining web-search roadmap](devel_docs/future-web-search.md) - [Provider and context feature backlog](devel_docs/future-provider-and-context-features.md) Deferred documents describe possible future work, not features in this release; the web-search roadmap separately identifies the implemented DeepSeek baseline. ## Development ```bash npm ci npm test npm run lint npm run build ``` Emend uses TypeScript, strict checks, Vitest, and esbuild. The plugin is desktop-only because its provider transport uses browser `fetch` with Server-Sent Events. ## Attribution Emend is based on Lapis Lazuli AI Assistant by Taha Yiğit Melek. See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md) and the MIT [LICENSE](LICENSE) for attribution. Maintained by **Chang Liu and Kimi K3.1 Pro**. This project was driven by vibecoding with **Kimi K3.1 Pro** using **Kimi Code**.

repository.readme:
# Keyhac 2 English \| [日本語](README.ja.md) Python-scriptable keyboard customization for **Windows and macOS**. Keyhac installs a system-wide keyboard hook and lets you script what your keys do in Python. You write one file, `~/.keyhac/config.py`, and it runs unchanged on both OSes — remapping keys, binding keys to Python functions, and driving windows, applications and the clipboard from the keyboard. It can also write the harder scripts for you. Connect an AI assistant and it reads the screen in front of you, generates a plain-Python action against the real UI, and tests it — then the action runs on its own, with no AI in the loop.

 

Keyhac 2 replaces the two previous-generation products, Keyhac for Windows (1.x) and Keyhac for macOS (1.x), rebuilt as one shared codebase. Those older versions are no longer developed — if you are coming from one of them, see the migration guides in [Documentation](#documentation) below. Keyhac 2's UI is built on [PuiKit](https://github.com/crftwr/puikit). ## Features - **Key remapping**: key → key, key → key sequence, key → Python function. - **Per-application key tables**: match by app name, window title, Win32 window class, or the full accessibility focus path (AX on macOS, UI Automation on Windows) — down to "only in this app's text editor pane". - **User modifiers**: turn any key into a modifier of your own (User0–User3), invisible to applications. - **One-shot modifiers**: tap a modifier alone for one action, hold it to modify. - **Multi-stroke key tables**: Emacs-style prefix keys, with a balloon showing the armed prefix. - **Clipboard history**: persistent history in a popup chooser — type to filter, Enter pastes into the app you came from, with its formatting, image or files; Option/Alt-Enter pastes plain text. Plus fixed snippets and scriptable clipboard-transform tools. - **Window control**: move, snap/tile, minimize, activate and launch applications, multi-monitor aware. - **Keyboard macros**: record and replay keys. - **Mouse output**: send clicks, wheel scrolls and pointer moves from key bindings. - **Extra Python libraries**: list them in `~/.keyhac/requirements.txt` and choose Advanced > Sync Python Packages in the tray menu — the app bundles included. - **Console window**: live log, last-key and focus-path inspector — see exactly what to bind. Runs from the system tray (Windows) / menu-bar extra (macOS). - **AI-authored actions**: let an AI assistant read the screen and write the automation for you, then bind it to a key — see [AI integration](#ai-integration) below. ## AI integration Keyhac can be driven by an AI assistant while you *write* your automation, and by nothing but Python once you run it. Connect Claude Desktop — or any MCP client — to Keyhac's local endpoint, and it can read the accessibility tree of the application in front of you, write an `Action` against the real element names it finds there, run it, read its own traceback, and fix it. No copy-pasting between a chat window and an editor. What you are left with is an ordinary Python class on a key: ```python import translate_clipboard def configure(keymap): kt = keymap.define_keytable(focus_path_pattern="*") kt["Fn-T"] = translate_clipboard.TranslateClipboard() ``` From then on it runs in milliseconds, offline, with no tokens and no model — the AI was the author, not the runtime. That matters most for applications with no API at all: walking pagination to the end, filling a form from each row of a CSV, reading tables out of an internal web app, capturing every settings screen to JSON. **It is off unless you turn it on** — a checkbox in the console window. The endpoint listens on loopback only, behind a token generated at startup, and closes itself an hour after you open it. [AI integration](doc/ai-integration.md) covers setup, which clients have been tried, what it can reach, and the security model. ## Screenshots | Console (macOS) | Console (Windows) | |---|---| | ![Keyhac console window on macOS: keyboard-hook toggle, log level selector, live key-event log, last-key and focus-path inspector](doc/images/console-mac.jpg) | ![Keyhac console window on Windows: keyboard-hook toggle, log level selector, live key-event log, last-key and focus-path inspector](doc/images/console-win.jpg) | | Menu-bar extra (macOS) | Task tray (Windows) | |---|---| | ![Keyhac menu-bar extra on macOS with its menu open: Open Console, Edit Config, Reload Config, Keyboard Hook, Quit Keyhac](doc/images/menubar-extra-icon-mac.jpg) | ![Keyhac task-tray icon on Windows with its menu open: Open Console, Edit Config, Reload Config, Keyboard Hook, Quit Keyhac](doc/images/tasktray-icon-win.jpg) | ## Install - **macOS 12+** — download `Keyhac--macos.dmg` from [Releases](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac/releases): drag Keyhac.app into Applications and launch it. Or install it with Homebrew: `brew install --cask crftwr/tap/keyhac`. Grant the Accessibility permission when prompted (required for the keyboard hook). - **Windows 10/11 (x64 and Arm)** — install from the [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9P8H1PG6PRHH) (or `winget install --id 9P8H1PG6PRHH --source msstore`) — automatic updates, no SmartScreen warning; the Store delivers the build that matches your device. Alternatively, download `Keyhac--win-x64.zip` (x64) or `Keyhac--win-arm64.zip` (Arm) from [Releases](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac/releases), unzip anywhere and run `Keyhac.exe`. Details, data locations and privacy notes: [doc/installation.md](doc/installation.md). ## Quick start On first run Keyhac creates `~/.keyhac/config.py` from a fully commented template. Open it from the tray / menu-bar icon ("Edit Config"), edit, then "Reload Config". A config defines one function: ```python from keyhac import * def configure(keymap): kt = keymap.define_keytable(focus_path_pattern="*") # active everywhere kt["Fn-J"] = "Left" # key -> key kt["Fn-A"] = "Home", "Shift-End" # key -> sequence def hello(): # key -> Python function print("Hello from config.py") kt["Fn-H"] = hello kt["Fn-V"] = ShowClipboardHistory() # clipboard history popup kt_browser = keymap.define_keytable(app="chrome|Safari") # per-app table kt_browser["Fn-R"] = "Cmd-R" ``` The full guide is [doc/configuration.md](doc/configuration.md), the per-symbol reference [doc/config-api.md](doc/config-api.md); the shipped template ([keyhac/_config.py](keyhac/_config.py)) is a working tour of every feature. ## Documentation - [Installation](doc/installation.md) — install, permissions, data files, privacy. - [Configuration](doc/configuration.md) — the complete config.py guide. - [API reference](doc/config-api.md) — every class and function a config.py can reach, with its exact arguments. - [AI integration](doc/ai-integration.md) — connect an MCP client, what the endpoint reaches, and the security model. - [Action API](doc/action-api.md) — the surface an action uses to drive another application: finding windows, searching element trees, waiting, filling fields. - [Migrating from Keyhac for macOS](doc/migration-from-keyhac-mac.md) — mostly drop-in. - [Migrating from Keyhac for Windows](doc/migration-from-keyhac-win.md) — API renamed; translation table. - Legacy products (no longer developed, kept for reference): [Keyhac for Windows 1.x](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac-win), [Keyhac for macOS 1.x](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac-mac). - [Developer documentation](doc/dev/) — architecture, platform layer, packaging, testing. Project guide for coding agents: [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). ## Running from source ```sh python3 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]" .venv/bin/python -m pytest # engine + unit tests, no permissions needed .venv/bin/python -m keyhac # run (macOS: needs Accessibility permission) ``` `python -m keyhac -d` enables debug logging, `--no-ui` runs headless (hook + engine only), `--config PATH` uses an alternate config file (its data files live beside it). ## Contact & Support - **GitHub Issues**: [Report bugs or request features](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac/issues/new/choose) - **GitHub Discussions**: [Questions, ideas, and configs or actions to share](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac/discussions) - **Security problems**: report privately — see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) - **Contributing**: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) - **PyPI**: [pypi.org/project/keyhac](https://pypi.org/project/keyhac/) — released versions - **Author's X (Twitter)**: [@crftwr](https://x.com/crftwr) ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

[AI integration](doc/ai-integration.md) covers setup, which clients have been tried, what it can reach, and the security model. ## Screenshots | Console (macOS) | Console (Windows) | |---|---| | ![Keyhac console window on macOS: keyboard-hook toggle, log level selector, live key-event log, last-key and focus-path inspector](doc/images/console-mac.jpg) | ![Keyhac console window on Windows: keyboard-hook toggle, log level selector, live key-event log, last-key and focus-path inspector](doc/images/console-win.jpg) | | Menu-bar extra (macOS) | Task tray (Windows) | |---|---| | ![Keyhac menu-bar extra on macOS with its menu open: Open Console, Edit Config, Reload Config, Keyboard Hook, Quit Keyhac](doc/images/menubar-extra-icon-mac.jpg) | ![Keyhac task-tray icon on Windows with its menu open: Open Console, Edit Config, Reload Config, Keyboard Hook, Quit Keyhac](doc/images/tasktray-icon-win.jpg) | ## Install - **macOS 12+** — download `Keyhac--macos.dmg` from [Releases](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac/releases): drag Keyhac.app into Applications and launch it. Or install it with Homebrew: `brew install --cask crftwr/tap/keyhac`. Grant the Accessibility permission when prompted (required for the keyboard hook). - **Windows 10/11 (x64 and Arm)** — install from the [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9P8H1PG6PRHH) (or `winget install --id 9P8H1PG6PRHH --source msstore`) — automatic updates, no SmartScreen warning; the Store delivers the build that matches your device. Alternatively, download `Keyhac--win-x64.zip` (x64) or `Keyhac--win-arm64.zip` (Arm) from [Releases](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac/releases), unzip anywhere and run `Keyhac.exe`. Details, data locations and privacy notes: [doc/installation.md](doc/installation.md). ## Quick start On first run Keyhac creates `~/.keyhac/config.py` from a fully commented template. Open it from the tray / menu-bar icon ("Edit Config"), edit, then "Reload Config". A config defines one function: ```python from keyhac import * def configure(keymap): kt = keymap.define_keytable(focus_path_pattern="*") # active everywhere kt["Fn-J"] = "Left" # key -> key kt["Fn-A"] = "Home", "Shift-End" # key -> sequence def hello(): # key -> Python function print("Hello from config.py") kt["Fn-H"] = hello kt["Fn-V"] = ShowClipboardHistory() # clipboard history popup kt_browser = keymap.define_keytable(app="chrome|Safari") # per-app table kt_browser["Fn-R"] = "Cmd-R" ``` The full guide is [doc/configuration.md](doc/configuration.md), the per-symbol reference [doc/config-api.md](doc/config-api.md); the shipped template ([keyhac/_config.py](keyhac/_config.py)) is a working tour of every feature. ## Documentation - [Installation](doc/installation.md) — install, permissions, data files, privacy. - [Configuration](doc/configuration.md) — the complete config.py guide. - [API reference](doc/config-api.md) — every class and function a config.py can reach, with its exact arguments. - [AI integration](doc/ai-integration.md) — connect an MCP client, what the endpoint reaches, and the security model. - [Action API](doc/action-api.md) — the surface an action uses to drive another application: finding windows, searching element trees, waiting, filling fields. - [Migrating from Keyhac for macOS](doc/migration-from-keyhac-mac.md) — mostly drop-in. - [Migrating from Keyhac for Windows](doc/migration-from-keyhac-win.md) — API renamed; translation table. - Legacy products (no longer developed, kept for reference): [Keyhac for Windows 1.x](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac-win), [Keyhac for macOS 1.x](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac-mac). - [Developer documentation](doc/dev/) — architecture, platform layer, packaging, testing. Project guide for coding agents: [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). ## Running from source ```sh python3 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]" .venv/bin/python -m pytest # engine + unit tests, no permissions needed .venv/bin/python -m keyhac # run (macOS: needs Accessibility permission) ``` `python -m keyhac -d` enables debug logging, `--no-ui` runs headless (hook + engine only), `--config PATH` uses an alternate config file (its data files live beside it). ## Contact & Support - **GitHub Issues**: [Report bugs or request features](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac/issues/new/choose) - **GitHub Discussions**: [Questions, ideas, and configs or actions to share](https://github.com/crftwr/keyhac/discussions) - **Security problems**: report privately — see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) - **Contributing**: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) - **PyPI**: [pypi.org/project/keyhac](https://pypi.org/project/keyhac/) — released versions - **Author's X (Twitter)**: [@crftwr](https://x.com/crftwr) ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "keyhac"
description = "Keyhac 2 - Python-scriptable keyboard customization tool for Windows and macOS"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = "MIT"
authors = [{ name = "craftware" }]
keywords = ["keyboard", "hotkey", "keymap", "macro", "remap", "customization",
            "automation", "ui-automation", "accessibility", "mcp", "ai"]
# version -> single-sourced from keyhac/__init__.py's __version__.
# readme -> README.pypi.md, generated on the fly by `make build`
# (tools/gen_pypi_readme.py): README.md with its repo-relative image/link
# targets rewritten to version-tagged GitHub URLs, so they render on the PyPI
# page, which has no repository to resolve them against. Both resolve in
# [tool.setuptools.dynamic] below.
dynamic = ["version", "readme"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Environment :: MacOS X",
    "Environment :: Win32 (MS Windows)",
    "Intended Audience :: End Users/Desktop",
    "Operating System :: MacOS",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Utilities",
]
dependencies = [
    # 1.4.2 is the first release with every puikit API/fix keyhac uses. What
    # the floor last moved for: 1.20.2, where a closed window and a dead raster
    # let go of their memory. Before it the chooser leaked on macOS for as long
    # as Keyhac ran, every open and close and every preview it showed
    # (issue #325).
    #
    # Before that: the four things a window drawing its own
    # chrome cannot work out for itself (PR #132) - pointer_position_px(),
    # because a mouse event's position is measured against a window that the
    # gesture is itself moving; set_frame_px(), because a resize from the top
    # or left edge has to move and resize in one step or the edge under the
    # hand twitches; corner_radius_px, because a border drawn square at the
    # window's extent loses exactly the four corners the platform clips; and
    # WindowStyle(movable=False), because macOS goes on dragging the window
    # by the title bar `frameless` only hides, so the chooser's own drag
    # handle would otherwise get both gestures at once.
    #
    # Before that: WindowHandle.resize_to_px (PR #131), without which the
    # chooser cannot be resized at all - it is frameless, which is what makes
    # it non-activating, and a frameless window has no edge for the user to
    # drag, so the grip it draws itself is the only one there is (issue #117).
    #
    # Before that: mark_screen() and ScreenMarker (PR #130,
    # capability screen_markers). The balloon and the outline the chooser puts
    # around the control it is pointing at are screen marks now, and on an
    # older puikit both are the base's already-closed mark - on Windows they
    # did not appear at all, so multi-stroke help and macro status were a
    # feature lost rather than degraded. The same release stops a lone
    # surrogate raising out of a paint on Windows, which is what a control
    # name truncated by UTF-16 units does to the row listing it. Earlier
    # floors, still required: WindowStyle's overlay_input (PR #126), without
    # which a click on the chooser activates Keyhac and deactivates the very
    # window the paste is aimed at; ListView(allow_no_selection=), for a list
    # that proposes no row while the filter field holds the focus; the
    # per-window pointer shape that stopped the cursor flickering between the
    # chooser and the console; set_tray(image=) (PR #82), main-window
    # visibility (PR #84), the LogView sized-font clip fix the 11pt console
    # log needs (PR #86), per-window IME input contexts (PR #90, issue #20 -
    # for the windows that still take keyboard focus; the chooser deliberately
    # no longer does) - and ListView scrolling an assigned selection into view
    # (PR #95), which keeps the chooser's highlight on screen (issue #27). To
    # develop against a local checkout, set PUIKIT_DIR (see Makefile).
    "puikit>=1.22.0",
    'pyobjc-framework-Cocoa>=10; sys_platform == "darwin"',
    'pyobjc-framework-Quartz>=10; sys_platform == "darwin"',
    'pyobjc-framework-ApplicationServices>=10; sys_platform == "darwin"',
    # HTTPS verified by the OS - Security.framework on macOS, CryptoAPI on
    # Windows - instead of OpenSSL against a static PEM file, so a revoked
    # certificate is refused and Keychain / certificate-store roots are
    # trusted (issue #279, keyhac/tls.py). Keyhac.app's python.org Python
    # otherwise looks for a CA file outside the app, missing on a Mac without
    # that Python. Pure Python on ctypes.
    'truststore>=0.10; sys_platform == "darwin" or sys_platform == "win32"',
    # Romaji-finds-Japanese filtering in the chooser (issue #106).  Pinned
    # rather than floated: keyhac/core/migemo.py carries a runtime patch for a
    # dictionary bug in 0.0.1 that reaches into the package's internals, so a
    # new release must be reviewed before it is taken.  Pure Python, BSD-3,
    # dictionary bundled in the wheel - no native library and no separate
    # dictionary placement for the user.
    #
    # A hard dependency, not an extra: the chooser does not take OS keyboard
    # focus, so it cannot host an input method, and without Migemo a localised
    # candidate list cannot be filtered by name at all.
    "pymigemo==0.0.1",
    # The chooser preview decodes clipboard images (PNG/TIFF/BMP bytes) into a
    # puikit RasterImage, scaled to fit (issue #262). puikit depends on it
    # already; named here because Keyhac imports it itself.
    "pillow>=9",
]

# quality-loop runs qa/ (`make qa`): the skill bundle tried by an isolated

dev = ["pytest>=8", "quality-loop>=0.5.0"]

[project.scripts]

# The stdio shim an MCP client spawns; it forwards to the running daemon.
keyhac-mcp-bridge = "keyhac.mcp.bridge:main"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://crftwr.github.io/keyhac/"

[tool.setuptools]
packages = [
    "keyhac",
    "keyhac.core",
    "keyhac.mcp",
    "keyhac.platform",
    "keyhac.platform.mac",

]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
# Runtime images loaded from keyhac/ui/assets at import time: the tray/menu-bar
# icons (keyhac/ui/tray.py) plus the .icns/.ico the bundle builders compile in.
# Without this the wheel ships bare .py files and a pip-installed Keyhac has no
# tray icon files to load.
"keyhac.ui" = ["assets/*"]
# The skill (keyhac/skills/keyhac). It ships with the
# package deliberately: it documents this exact version's API, and a skill that
# has drifted from the API it describes is worse than no skill. Not an
# importable package - the directory name is hyphenated and it holds Markdown -
# so it rides along as data on `keyhac` itself.
# The skill and nothing else: SKILL.md and its references, which is what the
# skill bundle carries too. Its evals used to sit in the same tree and rode
# into the wheel on broader globs (issue #190); they are development tooling
# and now live with the clean room in .claude/skills/.
"keyhac" = ["skills/*/SKILL.md", "skills/*/references/*.md"]

[tool.setuptools.exclude-package-data]
# Addressed to whoever works on Keyhac (why three references are copied in at
# bundle time), not to a reader of the skill - the bundle leaves it out too.
"keyhac" = ["skills/*/references/README.md"]

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = { attr = "keyhac.__version__" }
# Generated by tools/gen_pypi_readme.py (make build), gitignored, and
# tolerated when absent: a plain `pip install -e .` without `make build` just
# gets an empty description in its local metadata, which nothing reads. The
# `twine check --strict` in `make build` keeps an empty description from ever
# reaching an upload.
readme = { file = ["README.pypi.md"], content-type = "text/markdown" }

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# quality-loop's plugin gives the desktop mark (skipped unless --desktop,
# which is for a VM) and host_only (skipped in a guest) - #316.
addopts = ["-p", "quality_loop.pytest_plugin"]
markers = [
    "slow: drives a real third-party app (launches it, waits on its UI); run with -m 'not slow' to skip",
]

repository.name: openrouter-uptime
repository.readme: # OpenRouter Uptime An independent, git-timestamped uptime registry for **every model on [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai)** and each of its inference providers. Two independent collectors poll OpenRouter's public API every 15 minutes -- a Railway cron as the primary and a GitHub Action as the fallback, each standing down when the other has polled recently. Every run saves the raw responses, records the status of every routing endpoint (~1,150 across ~400 catalog models) plus provider metadata, and commits the result. Every poll is a timestamped snapshot in `raw/` and `derived/`, so any endpoint's availability can be reconstructed over time from the files themselves. Measured sampling characteristics -- duty cycle, gaps, per-hour density -- are published in [`status/coverage.json`](status/coverage.json). No API key required. Everything comes from OpenRouter's public endpoints. **Mirrors:** this repo is the source of truth; a tidy Parquet copy is refreshed daily on [HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/datasets/venvoo/openrouter-uptime) and [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/spicycorn/openrouter-uptime). ## What's in here Three committed folders: `raw/` (verbatim archives), `derived/` (tidy CSVs), `status/` (current snapshots and change logs). | path | contents | |---|---| | `raw/YYYY-MM-DD/HHMMSS.json.gz` | ground truth: the verbatim `/models`, `/providers` (formerly `/all-providers`), and every `/endpoints` API response for that run. Everything below is derived from these and can be rebuilt with `scripts/reparse.py`. | | `derived/YYYY-MM-DD.csv` | one row per endpoint per poll: `ts, model, provider, endpoint_tag, endpoint_id, identity_ambiguous, state, status, up5m, up30m, up1d`. Endpoint identity is `(model, endpoint_id)` — provider name alone is not unique, since one provider can serve several endpoints for the same model. `endpoint_id` is the tag when it is unique; duplicate tags carry a `#fingerprint` of their descriptive fields, and endpoints indistinguishable even by that carry a further `#N` in array order (Baseten has published such pairs since 2026-09-01). Rows with `identity_ambiguous=true` are real readings but not a longitudinal series: the suffix is not stable across polls, and `incidents.jsonl` skips them. `state` is `unknown` when the endpoint fetch itself failed. | | `status/latest.json` | most recent full endpoint snapshot | | `status/incidents.jsonl` | append-only outage log; each line is an endpoint transition that touches `down` (note `recovered` can mean down→degraded, not necessarily full health — check `to`). Carries `previous_ts`, `observation_gap` and `minutes_since_last_seen`, so transitions bridged across sampling gaps are marked rather than silent. Rebuilt verbatim from `raw/` by `scripts/rebuild_history.py`; `scripts/audit.py` fails if the two ever differ | | `status/models.json` | live model catalog, refreshed every run (on catalog-fetch failure the last good snapshot is reused and uptime readings continue) | | `status/model_changes.jsonl` | append-only log of models added to or removed from OpenRouter, plus catalog fetch outages | | `status/providers.json` | each provider's metadata (HQ, ToS/privacy/status-page URLs). Until 2026-07-15 it also carried OpenRouter's reported data policy (training, prompt retention, moderation); upstream stopped publishing it, so `data_policy` is null after that date (last-known values remain in `raw/`) | | `status/provider_changes.jsonl` | append-only log of providers added/removed, data-policy edits (pre-2026-07-15), ToS/privacy/status-page URL edits, and fetch outages (the providers surface is best-effort; uptime readings continue through its failures) | The README's **Systemic events** section (below) is regenerated every run by `scripts/readme_events.py`: it surfaces only fleet-level signals from those logs — batch catalog changes (>=3 models in one poll), provider exits, fetch outages, and upstream schema breaks — and skips per-model churn. **State** comes from OpenRouter's 30-minute uptime figure: `up` (>=98%), `degraded` (50 to 98%), `down` (<50% or non-OK status), `idle` (no recent traffic, not a fault). ## Why raw is kept The derived CSV/JSON reflect one interpretation of the API. If that parsing is ever wrong, or we later want a field we didn't extract, `raw/` holds the complete original response for every run, so nothing is lost to a parser bug. `python3 scripts/reparse.py raw/.../HHMMSS.json.gz` regenerates the derived rows from any archive. ## Use the data ```bash grep anthropic/claude-sonnet derived/$(date -u +%F).csv # one model, today jq 'select(.event=="down")' status/incidents.jsonl # every outage start python3 scripts/reparse.py raw/2026-07-04/140117.json.gz # rebuild from raw ls raw/ # one folder per day ``` ## Notes - Keyless: `poll.py` uses only OpenRouter's public API. - Schedulers are best-effort; the `ts` column records the true poll time, and `status/coverage.json` records what was actually achieved. Until 2026-08-06 the collector ran hourly at best (21.6% duty cycle for the 30-minute window); judge the early series by the coverage file, not the schedule. - Raw archives are ~160 KB gzipped per run (~15 MB/day at the 15-min cadence). - OpenRouter's uptime figures are its own measurements of its routing layer. - Built to study AI-infrastructure dependence; contributions welcome. ## Current status (2026-11-07T06:30:57+00:00 UTC) 460 models polled, 1519 inference endpoints: up 1012, degraded 38, down 32, idle 437. Currently down (32): | model | endpoint | provider | 30m uptime | 5m uptime | |---|---|---|---|---| | `amazon/nova-premier-v1` | `amazon-bedrock` | Amazon Bedrock | 0% | 0% | | `deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1` | `sambanova/fp8` | SambaNova | n/a | n/a | | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `deepinfra/fp8/flex` | DeepInfra | 0% | 0% | | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | `sail-research/fp4/us` | Sail Research | 0% | n/a | | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | `sail-research/fp4` | Sail Research | n/a | n/a | | `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | `google-ai-studio/priority` | Google AI Studio | 46% | 100% | | `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 21% | n/a | | `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 0% | n/a | | `google/gemini-3.6-flash` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 17% | n/a | | `google/gemini-3.7-flash` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 0% | n/a | | `google/gemini-3.8-flash` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 42% | 75% | | `google/lyria-3-pro-preview` | `google-ai-studio` | Google AI Studio | 100% | n/a | | `inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash` | `deepinfra/bf16` | DeepInfra | 74% | 0% | | `liquid/lfm-3-1.7b` | `liquid/fp8` | Liquid | 13% | 40% | | `moonshotai/kimi-k3` | `fireworks/fast` | Fireworks | 71% | 0% | | plus 17 more | | | | | Full snapshot: [`status/latest.json`](status/latest.json). Outage log: [`status/incidents.jsonl`](status/incidents.jsonl). ### Systemic events _Fleet-level changes extracted from the change logs every run; per-model churn is omitted._ - **2026-10-26 22:01** — **5 models removed from the catalog in one poll**: `mistralai/codestral-2508:batch`, `mistralai/ministral-8b-2512:batch`, `mistralai/mistral-large-2512:batch`, `mistralai/mistral-medium-3.1:batch`, `mistralai/mistral-small-2603:batch`. - **2026-10-28 15:03** — **8 models removed from the catalog in one poll**: `openai/gpt-4-turbo`, `openai/o1`, `openai/o1-pro`, `openai/o3-mini`, `openai/o3-mini-high`, `openai/o4-mini`, `openai/o4-mini-high`, `qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-thinking`. - **2026-10-28 18:31** — provider `primalabs` changed its terms of service url. - **2026-10-28 18:31** — provider `primalabs` changed its privacy policy url. - **2026-10-28 18:31** — provider `primalabs` changed its status page. - **2026-10-31 13:16** — **4 models removed from the catalog in one poll**: `poolside/laguna-s-2.1`, `poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free`, `poolside/laguna-xs-2.1`, `poolside/laguna-xs-2.1:free`. - **2026-11-02 23:46** — provider `kt` changed its terms of service url. - **2026-11-02 23:46** — provider `kt` changed its privacy policy url. - **2026-11-04 16:47** — provider `antdigital` changed its terms of service url. - **2026-11-04 16:47** — provider `antdigital` changed its privacy policy url. - **2026-11-05 13:16** — **4 models removed from the catalog in one poll**: `minimax/minimax-01`, `minimax/minimax-m2`, `minimax/minimax-m2-her`, `minimax/minimax-m2.1`. - **2026-11-06 19:01** — **4 models added to the catalog in one poll**: `meta/muse-glimmer-30b:batch`, `minimax/minimax-m3:batch`, `qwen/qwen3.8-27b:batch`, `thinkingmachines/inkling-small:batch`. Full logs: [`status/model_changes.jsonl`](status/model_changes.jsonl), [`status/provider_changes.jsonl`](status/provider_changes.jsonl).

name: test

# Runs only when collector code changes. The pollers commit data to main every
# fifteen minutes; a push trigger without the paths filter would burn a CI run
# on every one of those commits for code that did not change.
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - "scripts/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - ".github/workflows/test.yml"
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Unit tests
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

      - name: Scripts compile
        run: python3 -m py_compile scripts/*.py

Every run saves the raw responses, records the status of every routing endpoint (~1,150 across ~400 catalog models) plus provider metadata, and commits the result. Every poll is a timestamped snapshot in `raw/` and `derived/`, so any endpoint's availability can be reconstructed over time from the files themselves. Measured sampling characteristics -- duty cycle, gaps, per-hour density -- are published in [`status/coverage.json`](status/coverage.json). No API key required. Everything comes from OpenRouter's public endpoints. **Mirrors:** this repo is the source of truth; a tidy Parquet copy is refreshed daily on [HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/datasets/venvoo/openrouter-uptime) and [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/spicycorn/openrouter-uptime). ## What's in here Three committed folders: `raw/` (verbatim archives), `derived/` (tidy CSVs), `status/` (current snapshots and change logs). | path | contents | |---|---| | `raw/YYYY-MM-DD/HHMMSS.json.gz` | ground truth: the verbatim `/models`, `/providers` (formerly `/all-providers`), and every `/endpoints` API response for that run. Everything below is derived from these and can be rebuilt with `scripts/reparse.py`. | | `derived/YYYY-MM-DD.csv` | one row per endpoint per poll: `ts, model, provider, endpoint_tag, endpoint_id, identity_ambiguous, state, status, up5m, up30m, up1d`. Endpoint identity is `(model, endpoint_id)` — provider name alone is not unique, since one provider can serve several endpoints for the same model. `endpoint_id` is the tag when it is unique; duplicate tags carry a `#fingerprint` of their descriptive fields, and endpoints indistinguishable even by that carry a further `#N` in array order (Baseten has published such pairs since 2026-09-01). Rows with `identity_ambiguous=true` are real readings but not a longitudinal series: the suffix is not stable across polls, and `incidents.jsonl` skips them. `state` is `unknown` when the endpoint fetch itself failed. | | `status/latest.json` | most recent full endpoint snapshot | | `status/incidents.jsonl` | append-only outage log; each line is an endpoint transition that touches `down` (note `recovered` can mean down→degraded, not necessarily full health — check `to`). Carries `previous_ts`, `observation_gap` and `minutes_since_last_seen`, so transitions bridged across sampling gaps are marked rather than silent. Rebuilt verbatim from `raw/` by `scripts/rebuild_history.py`; `scripts/audit.py` fails if the two ever differ | | `status/models.json` | live model catalog, refreshed every run (on catalog-fetch failure the last good snapshot is reused and uptime readings continue) | | `status/model_changes.jsonl` | append-only log of models added to or removed from OpenRouter, plus catalog fetch outages | | `status/providers.json` | each provider's metadata (HQ, ToS/privacy/status-page URLs). Until 2026-07-15 it also carried OpenRouter's reported data policy (training, prompt retention, moderation); upstream stopped publishing it, so `data_policy` is null after that date (last-known values remain in `raw/`) | | `status/provider_changes.jsonl` | append-only log of providers added/removed, data-policy edits (pre-2026-07-15), ToS/privacy/status-page URL edits, and fetch outages (the providers surface is best-effort; uptime readings continue through its failures) | The README's **Systemic events** section (below) is regenerated every run by `scripts/readme_events.py`: it surfaces only fleet-level signals from those logs — batch catalog changes (>=3 models in one poll), provider exits, fetch outages, and upstream schema breaks — and skips per-model churn. **State** comes from OpenRouter's 30-minute uptime figure: `up` (>=98%), `degraded` (50 to 98%), `down` (<50% or non-OK status), `idle` (no recent traffic, not a fault). ## Why raw is kept The derived CSV/JSON reflect one interpretation of the API. If that parsing is ever wrong, or we later want a field we didn't extract, `raw/` holds the complete original response for every run, so nothing is lost to a parser bug. `python3 scripts/reparse.py raw/.../HHMMSS.json.gz` regenerates the derived rows from any archive. ## Use the data ```bash grep anthropic/claude-sonnet derived/$(date -u +%F).csv # one model, today jq 'select(.event=="down")' status/incidents.jsonl # every outage start python3 scripts/reparse.py raw/2026-07-04/140117.json.gz # rebuild from raw ls raw/ # one folder per day ``` ## Notes - Keyless: `poll.py` uses only OpenRouter's public API. - Schedulers are best-effort; the `ts` column records the true poll time, and `status/coverage.json` records what was actually achieved. Until 2026-08-06 the collector ran hourly at best (21.6% duty cycle for the 30-minute window); judge the early series by the coverage file, not the schedule. - Raw archives are ~160 KB gzipped per run (~15 MB/day at the 15-min cadence). - OpenRouter's uptime figures are its own measurements of its routing layer. - Built to study AI-infrastructure dependence; contributions welcome. ## Current status (2026-11-07T06:30:57+00:00 UTC) 460 models polled, 1519 inference endpoints: up 1012, degraded 38, down 32, idle 437. Currently down (32): | model | endpoint | provider | 30m uptime | 5m uptime | |---|---|---|---|---| | `amazon/nova-premier-v1` | `amazon-bedrock` | Amazon Bedrock | 0% | 0% | | `deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1` | `sambanova/fp8` | SambaNova | n/a | n/a | | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `deepinfra/fp8/flex` | DeepInfra | 0% | 0% | | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | `sail-research/fp4/us` | Sail Research | 0% | n/a | | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | `sail-research/fp4` | Sail Research | n/a | n/a | | `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | `google-ai-studio/priority` | Google AI Studio | 46% | 100% | | `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 21% | n/a | | `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 0% | n/a | | `google/gemini-3.6-flash` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 17% | n/a | | `google/gemini-3.7-flash` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 0% | n/a | | `google/gemini-3.8-flash` | `google-vertex/global/flex` | Google | 42% | 75% | | `google/lyria-3-pro-preview` | `google-ai-studio` | Google AI Studio | 100% | n/a | | `inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash` | `deepinfra/bf16` | DeepInfra | 74% | 0% | | `liquid/lfm-3-1.7b` | `liquid/fp8` | Liquid | 13% | 40% | | `moonshotai/kimi-k3` | `fireworks/fast` | Fireworks | 71% | 0% | | plus 17 more | | | | | Full snapshot: [`status/latest.json`](status/latest.json). Outage log: [`status/incidents.jsonl`](status/incidents.jsonl). ### Systemic events _Fleet-level changes extracted from the change logs every run; per-model churn is omitted._ - **2026-10-26 22:01** — **5 models removed from the catalog in one poll**: `mistralai/codestral-2508:batch`, `mistralai/ministral-8b-2512:batch`, `mistralai/mistral-large-2512:batch`, `mistralai/mistral-medium-3.1:batch`, `mistralai/mistral-small-2603:batch`. - **2026-10-28 15:03** — **8 models removed from the catalog in one poll**: `openai/gpt-4-turbo`, `openai/o1`, `openai/o1-pro`, `openai/o3-mini`, `openai/o3-mini-high`, `openai/o4-mini`, `openai/o4-mini-high`, `qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-thinking`. - **2026-10-28 18:31** — provider `primalabs` changed its terms of service url. - **2026-10-28 18:31** — provider `primalabs` changed its privacy policy url. - **2026-10-28 18:31** — provider `primalabs` changed its status page. - **2026-10-31 13:16** — **4 models removed from the catalog in one poll**: `poolside/laguna-s-2.1`, `poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free`, `poolside/laguna-xs-2.1`, `poolside/laguna-xs-2.1:free`. - **2026-11-02 23:46** — provider `kt` changed its terms of service url. - **2026-11-02 23:46** — provider `kt` changed its privacy policy url. - **2026-11-04 16:47** — provider `antdigital` changed its terms of service url. - **2026-11-04 16:47** — provider `antdigital` changed its privacy policy url. - **2026-11-05 13:16** — **4 models removed from the catalog in one poll**: `minimax/minimax-01`, `minimax/minimax-m2`, `minimax/minimax-m2-her`, `minimax/minimax-m2.1`. - **2026-11-06 19:01** — **4 models added to the catalog in one poll**: `meta/muse-glimmer-30b:batch`, `minimax/minimax-m3:batch`, `qwen/qwen3.8-27b:batch`, `thinkingmachines/inkling-small:batch`.
