repository.readme:
# Intervals.icu MCP Server ![intervals-icu-mcp demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/main/docs/demo.gif) A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Intervals.icu integration. Access your training data, wellness metrics, and performance analysis through Claude, ChatGPT, and other LLMs. > Originally based on [eddmann/intervals-icu-mcp](https://github.com/eddmann/intervals-icu-mcp) (MIT licensed). This project is an independent continuation with significant bug fixes and new features — see the [release notes](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/releases) for details. [![Tests](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![intervals-icu-mcp MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/docker-ghcr.io-blue?logo=docker)](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/pkgs/container/intervals-icu-mcp) [![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/badge/sponsor-%E2%9D%A4-ff69b4?logo=githubsponsors)](https://github.com/sponsors/hhopke) ## Overview 73 tools spanning activities, activity analysis, activity messages, athlete profile, wellness, events/calendar, performance curves, workout library, gear, sport settings, and custom items — plus 4 MCP Resources (athlete profile, workout syntax, event categories, custom item schemas) and 9 MCP Prompts (training analysis, recovery check, weekly planning, and more). See [Available Tools](#available-tools) for the per-category breakdown. ## Quick Start Or for Claude Desktop, in 30 seconds: 1. Get your [API key and athlete ID](#intervalsicu-api-key-setup) 2. Add this to your Claude Desktop config: ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["intervals-icu-mcp"], "env": { "INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here", "INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID": "i123456" } } } } ``` 3. Restart Claude and ask *"Show me my activities from the last 7 days."* Prefer Claude Code, Cursor, or ChatGPT? See [Client Configuration](#client-configuration). Want to run from source or with Docker? See [Installation & Setup](#installation--setup). ## Prerequisites Install [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) — it handles Python, dependencies, and execution in one tool. `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` on macOS/Linux (or `brew install uv`; Homebrew no longer installs on Intel Macs), or `powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"` on Windows. From there, `uvx` fetches Python and the package automatically. If your MCP client can't find `uvx`, set `command` to the full path that `which uvx` prints. Docker is also supported as an alternative. ## Intervals.icu API Key Setup Before installation, obtain your Intervals.icu API key: 1. Go to https://intervals.icu/settings → **Developer** → **Create API Key**. 2. Copy the key, and note your **Athlete ID** from your profile URL (format: `i123456`). ## Installation & Setup **Nothing to install separately if you use the recommended setup.** `uvx` (which ships with `uv`) automatically downloads and caches the `intervals-icu-mcp` package the first time your MCP client launches it — just paste the config snippet from [Client Configuration](#client-configuration) into your client and you're done.
Alternative: from source — for development or local modifications ```bash git clone https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp.git cd intervals-icu-mcp uv sync uv run intervals-icu-mcp-auth # interactive credential setup; or create .env manually: # INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY=your_api_key_here # INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID=i123456 ``` Then point your MCP client at this checkout — see the **From source** snippet inside each client below.
Alternative: Docker ```bash docker build -t intervals-icu-mcp . # Interactive credential setup (creates intervals-icu-mcp.env in the current directory): touch intervals-icu-mcp.env # pre-create the file so Docker mounts it as a file, not a dir docker run -it --rm \ -v "$(pwd)/intervals-icu-mcp.env:/app/.env" \ --entrypoint= intervals-icu-mcp:latest \ python -m intervals_icu_mcp.scripts.setup_auth ``` Or create `intervals-icu-mcp.env` manually (same format as the `.env` above). Then point your MCP client at the Docker image — see the **Docker** snippet inside each client below.
## Client Configuration The server speaks MCP over stdio and works with any compliant client. Click a client to expand. If you followed Quick Start (uvx), use the first config block; if you used the source or Docker alternative above, use the matching variant inside the same collapsible.
Claude Desktop Add to your configuration file: - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` - Windows: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["intervals-icu-mcp"], "env": { "INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here", "INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID": "i123456" } } } } ``` **From source** (requires `git clone` + `uv sync` + `uv run intervals-icu-mcp-auth`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--directory", "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/intervals-icu-mcp", "intervals-icu-mcp"] } } } ``` **Docker**: ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "docker", "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "-v", "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/intervals-icu-mcp.env:/app/.env", "intervals-icu-mcp:latest"] } } } ```
Claude Code Register the server as a user-scoped MCP server: ```bash claude mcp add intervals-icu --scope user \ --env INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY=your-key \ --env INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID=i123456 \ -- uvx intervals-icu-mcp ``` Then in any Claude Code session, run `/mcp` to confirm `intervals-icu` is connected.
Cursor Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (or the project-local `.cursor/mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["intervals-icu-mcp"], "env": { "INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here", "INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID": "i123456" } } } } ``` Restart Cursor and open *Settings → MCP* to verify the server is listed.
ChatGPT — requires a paid plan, Developer Mode, and a publicly reachable URL (walkthrough not yet verified end-to-end) ChatGPT's custom MCP connector flow requires running the server over HTTP and exposing it via a tunnel, then registering the URL in ChatGPT's Developer Mode settings. See [docs/chatgpt-connector.md](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/blob/main/docs/chatgpt-connector.md) for the full walkthrough, plan-tier requirements, and security notes.
## Usage Ask Claude to interact with your Intervals.icu data in natural language. A few starter prompts: ``` "Show me my activities from the last 30 days" "Am I overtraining? Check my CTL, ATL, and TSB" "How's my recovery this week? Show HRV and sleep trends" "Create a sweet spot cycling workout for tomorrow" "What's my 20-minute power and FTP?" ``` For the full catalogue of example prompts by category, see [docs/examples.md](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/blob/main/docs/examples.md). ## Available Tools 73 tools, 4 resources, and 9 prompt templates. name: Test

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_call:

jobs:
  test:
    name: Run Tests (Python ${{ matrix.python-version }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ['3.11', '3.12', '3.13', '3.14', '3.15']

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync

      - name: Run linting (ruff)
        run: uv run ruff check

      - name: Run type checking (pyright)
        run: uv run pyright

      - name: Run tests
        run: >
          uv run pytest
          --cov=src/intervals_icu_mcp
          --cov-report=term-missing
          --cov-fail-under=80

  package:
    name: Validate package metadata and doc files
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      - name: Validate PyPI metadata and README rendering
        run: make lint/package

      - name: Verify internal doc files exist
        run: |
          test -f CHANGELOG.md
          test -f docs/tools.md
          test -f docs/examples.md
          test -f docs/architecture.md
          test -f docs/testing.md
          test -f .claude/skills/add-tool/SKILL.md

  all-green:
    # Single stable context for branch protection — survives matrix changes.
    # `if: always()` because a skipped job would satisfy a required check.
    name: All checks green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [test, package]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all jobs succeeded
        run: |
          test "${{ needs.test.result }}" = "success"
          test "${{ needs.package.result }}" = "success"

# Multi-stage build for minimal final image
FROM --platform=$TARGETPLATFORM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.7 AS uv

FROM --platform=$TARGETPLATFORM python:3.14-slim AS builder

# Install uv for faster dependency management
COPY --from=uv /uv /usr/local/bin/uv

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Version is derived from git via hatch-vcs at build time, but the .git
# directory is not in the Docker build context. The CI workflow builds a
# wheel locally to compute the version and passes it through as a build-arg.
ARG PKG_VERSION=0.0.0+docker
ENV SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=$PKG_VERSION

# Copy dependency files and README (needed for package metadata)
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock* README.md ./

# Copy source code (needed for building the package)
COPY src/ ./src/

# Install dependencies into a virtual environment
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev

# Final stage - minimal runtime image
FROM --platform=$TARGETPLATFORM python:3.14-slim

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy virtual environment from builder
COPY --from=builder /app/.venv /app/.venv

# Copy application code
COPY src/ ./src/
COPY pyproject.toml ./

# Set environment variables
ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH" \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1

# Health check uses the stdlib liveness probe; its default timeout is 2 seconds.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD python -m intervals_icu_mcp.healthcheck

# Run the MCP server
ENTRYPOINT ["python", "-m", "intervals_icu_mcp.server"]

sampled_files.README.md:
# Intervals.icu MCP Server ![intervals-icu-mcp demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/main/docs/demo.gif) A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Intervals.icu integration. Access your training data, wellness metrics, and performance analysis through Claude, ChatGPT, and other LLMs. > Originally based on [eddmann/intervals-icu-mcp](https://github.com/eddmann/intervals-icu-mcp) (MIT licensed). This project is an independent continuation with significant bug fixes and new features — see the [release notes](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/releases) for details. [![Tests](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![intervals-icu-mcp MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/docker-ghcr.io-blue?logo=docker)](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/pkgs/container/intervals-icu-mcp) [![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/badge/sponsor-%E2%9D%A4-ff69b4?logo=githubsponsors)](https://github.com/sponsors/hhopke) ## Overview 73 tools spanning activities, activity analysis, activity messages, athlete profile, wellness, events/calendar, performance curves, workout library, gear, sport settings, and custom items — plus 4 MCP Resources (athlete profile, workout syntax, event categories, custom item schemas) and 9 MCP Prompts (training analysis, recovery check, weekly planning, and more). See [Available Tools](#available-tools) for the per-category breakdown. ## Quick Start Or for Claude Desktop, in 30 seconds: 1. Get your [API key and athlete ID](#intervalsicu-api-key-setup) 2. Add this to your Claude Desktop config: ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["intervals-icu-mcp"], "env": { "INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here", "INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID": "i123456" } } } } ``` 3. Restart Claude and ask *"Show me my activities from the last 7 days."* Prefer Claude Code, Cursor, or ChatGPT? See [Client Configuration](#client-configuration). Want to run from source or with Docker? See [Installation & Setup](#installation--setup). ## Prerequisites Install [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) — it handles Python, dependencies, and execution in one tool. `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` on macOS/Linux (or `brew install uv`; Homebrew no longer installs on Intel Macs), or `powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"` on Windows. From there, `uvx` fetches Python and the package automatically. If your MCP client can't find `uvx`, set `command` to the full path that `which uvx` prints. Docker is also supported as an alternative. ## Intervals.icu API Key Setup Before installation, obtain your Intervals.icu API key: 1. Go to https://intervals.icu/settings → **Developer** → **Create API Key**. 2. Copy the key, and note your **Athlete ID** from your profile URL (format: `i123456`). ## Installation & Setup **Nothing to install separately if you use the recommended setup.** `uvx` (which ships with `uv`) automatically downloads and caches the `intervals-icu-mcp` package the first time your MCP client launches it — just paste the config snippet from [Client Configuration](#client-configuration) into your client and you're done.
Alternative: from source — for development or local modifications ```bash git clone https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp.git cd intervals-icu-mcp uv sync uv run intervals-icu-mcp-auth # interactive credential setup; or create .env manually: # INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY=your_api_key_here # INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID=i123456 ``` Then point your MCP client at this checkout — see the **From source** snippet inside each client below.
Alternative: Docker ```bash docker build -t intervals-icu-mcp . # Interactive credential setup (creates intervals-icu-mcp.env in the current directory): touch intervals-icu-mcp.env # pre-create the file so Docker mounts it as a file, not a dir docker run -it --rm \ -v "$(pwd)/intervals-icu-mcp.env:/app/.env" \ --entrypoint= intervals-icu-mcp:latest \ python -m intervals_icu_mcp.scripts.setup_auth ``` Or create `intervals-icu-mcp.env` manually (same format as the `.env` above). Then point your MCP client at the Docker image — see the **Docker** snippet inside each client below.
## Client Configuration The server speaks MCP over stdio and works with any compliant client. Click a client to expand. If you followed Quick Start (uvx), use the first config block; if you used the source or Docker alternative above, use the matching variant inside the same collapsible.
Claude Desktop Add to your configuration file: - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` - Windows: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["intervals-icu-mcp"], "env": { "INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here", "INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID": "i123456" } } } } ``` **From source** (requires `git clone` + `uv sync` + `uv run intervals-icu-mcp-auth`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--directory", "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/intervals-icu-mcp", "intervals-icu-mcp"] } } } ``` **Docker**: ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "docker", "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "-v", "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/intervals-icu-mcp.env:/app/.env", "intervals-icu-mcp:latest"] } } } ```
Claude Code Register the server as a user-scoped MCP server: ```bash claude mcp add intervals-icu --scope user \ --env INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY=your-key \ --env INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID=i123456 \ -- uvx intervals-icu-mcp ``` Then in any Claude Code session, run `/mcp` to confirm `intervals-icu` is connected.
Cursor Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (or the project-local `.cursor/mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "intervals-icu": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["intervals-icu-mcp"], "env": { "INTERVALS_ICU_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here", "INTERVALS_ICU_ATHLETE_ID": "i123456" } } } } ``` Restart Cursor and open *Settings → MCP* to verify the server is listed.
ChatGPT — requires a paid plan, Developer Mode, and a publicly reachable URL (walkthrough not yet verified end-to-end) ChatGPT's custom MCP connector flow requires running the server over HTTP and exposing it via a tunnel, then registering the URL in ChatGPT's Developer Mode settings. See [docs/chatgpt-connector.md](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/blob/main/docs/chatgpt-connector.md) for the full walkthrough, plan-tier requirements, and security notes.
## Usage Ask Claude to interact with your Intervals.icu data in natural language. A few starter prompts: ``` "Show me my activities from the last 30 days" "Am I overtraining? Check my CTL, ATL, and TSB" "How's my recovery this week? Show HRV and sleep trends" "Create a sweet spot cycling workout for tomorrow" "What's my 20-minute power and FTP?" ``` For the full catalogue of example prompts by category, see [docs/examples.md](https://github.com/hhopke/intervals-icu-mcp/blob/main/docs/examples.md). ## Available Tools 73 tools, 4 resources, and 9 prompt templates. repository.readme:
Cause the other agents piss me off.

English | 简体中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Español | Português | Deutsch | Français

GG Coder is a desktop coding agent that gets more out of the AI subscription you already pay for. > ⭐ **If GG Coder saves you time or money, give it a star.** It's the main way other developers find it. ## Why GG Coder - **More work per plan.** Fastest and leanest of 20 agents I raced on the same model. Claude Code used 169% more for the same work. - **Real code, not guesses.** Agent Steroids searches real, current open-source code on your machine. No rate-limited MCP server, no limits. - **Done means checked.** Ken Autopilot keeps the work going until it's actually verified. - **Ship it properly, even as a beginner.** Coding is only part of it. One-click checks for security, compliance, data safety, accessibility, tests and more, plus a Project health score, so you don't need to know what to ask for. - **Your subscriptions.** Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Kimi, API keys or local models. | Agent | Time for the full suite | Usage per suite | Time vs GG Coder | Usage vs GG Coder | | ------------------ | ----------------------- | --------------- | ---------------- | ----------------- | | **GG Coder** | **102 s** | **$0.014** | | | | Codewhale | 112 s | $0.022 | 10% slower | 58% more | | Goose | 132 s | $0.020 | 29% slower | 46% more | | GitHub Copilot CLI | 136 s | $0.025 | 33% slower | 83% more | | Kimi Code | 138 s | $0.024 | 36% slower | 74% more | | Claude Code | 142 s | $0.037 | 39% slower | 169% more | | ForgeCode | 155 s | $0.042 | 52% slower | 204% more | | Dirac | 160 s | $0.029 | 57% slower | 114% more | | Crush | 165 s | $0.037 | 62% slower | 173% more | | Factory Droid | 167 s | $0.025 | 64% slower | 83% more | | Mistral Vibe | 169 s | $0.036 | 66% slower | 164% more | | DeepSeek-Reasonix | 170 s | $0.027 | 67% slower | 99% more | | Oh My Pi | 170 s | $0.031 | 67% slower | 123% more | | Xum | 172 s | $0.041 | 69% slower | 203% more | | Docker Agent | 173 s | $0.021 | 70% slower | 51% more | | Qwen Code | 177 s | $0.049 | 74% slower | 257% more | | Prime Agent | 190 s | $0.029 | 86% slower | 111% more | | Hermes Agent | 190 s | $0.027 | 87% slower | 100% more | | Deep Agents | 201 s | $0.041 | 97% slower | 198% more | | jcode | 380 s | $0.178 | 274% slower | 1196% more | Table: one full race on 4 November 2026. 20 agents, each on a current stable release (GG Coder v0.102.0), 7 tasks, 5 runs each (700 runs), all on Claude Haiku 5.5 with the same thinking setting. Every agent got the same prompts and a fresh copy of the project each run, and ran bare, GG Coder included: its own built-in prompt and tools, with no skills, plugins, MCP servers or custom instructions. The tasks use small test projects plus one question about Vite's codebase (v8.3.5), so no agent works on its own code. A run counts only if hidden tests pass or the answer is correct. ## Also included - **GG Goals:** hand over a whole goal; a team of workers sees it through. - **Chat:** conversations that remember context. - **GG Motion:** turns your ideas into videos. ## Get started 1. Install GG Coder: **macOS (Apple Silicon):** [Download the latest release](https://github.com/KenKaiii/gg-framework/releases/latest) and open the `.dmg`. **Windows:** [Download the latest release](https://github.com/KenKaiii/gg-framework/releases/latest) and run the `.exe` installer. **Linux (x86_64):** [Download the latest release](https://github.com/KenKaiii/gg-framework/releases/latest) and install the `.deb` (`sudo apt install ./GG*.deb`) or `.rpm` (`sudo dnf install ./GG*.rpm`). **Development:** With Node.js, pnpm, and the [Tauri prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/) installed: ```bash git clone https://github.com/KenKaiii/gg-framework.git cd gg-framework pnpm install pnpm build pnpm --filter gg-app tauri dev ``` 2. Open the app, connect your AI provider, and pick Code, Chat, or Motion. ## Build with the framework Want the engine without the desktop app? Use the same packages in your own apps. Install just what you need. - [**@kenkaiiii/gg-ai**](packages/gg-ai/README.md): Connect to AI providers and stream responses. - [**@kenkaiiii/gg-agent**](packages/gg-agent/README.md): Build agents that use your tools and work through tasks. - [**@kenkaiiii/gg-core**](packages/gg-core/README.md): Model selection, authentication, and local model discovery. - [**@kenkaiiii/ggcoder**](packages/ggcoder/README.md): The coding agent, sessions, and tools behind the app and CLI. For your own agent, start here: ```bash npm install @kenkaiiii/gg-ai @kenkaiiii/gg-agent ``` The package links above cover setup and usage. Licensed under AGPL-3.0: you can build on it, and if you distribute your changes or run them as a network service, you share their source under the same license. ## Contributing Bug reports, ideas and pull requests are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before you start. ## Learn with me Come build with me in my [Skool community](https://skool.com/kenkai). Get help, share what you're making, and learn how to get more out of AI. ## Star history

If GG Coder is useful to you, ⭐ star the repo so more people find it.

sampled_files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

# Cancel the superseded run when a branch gets rapid successive pushes/PR
# updates. Keyed on head_ref for PRs, run_id (never collides) for main pushes.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Cross-platform smoke matrix. Every push to main and every PR runs build +
# typecheck + test + bin-smoke on macOS, Linux, and Windows so we catch
# platform-specific regressions before they hit npm.
#
# The framework release spine is gg-ai, gg-agent, gg-core, and ggcoder.

jobs:
  test:
    name: ${{ matrix.os }} · node ${{ matrix.node }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        node: [22.x]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # pnpm version comes from package.json's packageManager field.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # ripgrep is optional at runtime, but grep-parity.test.ts only compares
      # the rg path against the in-process scanner when `rg` is on PATH. None of
      # the runner images ship it, so without this the parity suite skipped on
      # every OS and proved nothing.
      - name: Install ripgrep (grep parity test)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
            Linux) sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ripgrep ;;
            macOS) HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew install ripgrep ;;
            Windows)
              # The Chocolatey community feed intermittently 504s, and choco
              # can exit 0 after installing nothing ("installed 0/0"), so
              # retry until `rg` actually exists; fail if every attempt fails.
              for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
                choco install ripgrep -y --no-progress || true
                if command -v rg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  break
                fi
                if [ "$attempt" -eq 4 ]; then
                  echo "choco install ripgrep failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
                  exit 1
                fi
                delay=$((attempt * 30))
                echo "choco install ripgrep failed (attempt $attempt); retrying in ${delay}s" >&2
                sleep "$delay"
              done
              ;;
          esac
          rg --version

      # `shell: bash` on EVERY multi-line step is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
      # On Windows the default shell is PowerShell, which does not abort a
      # multi-line script when an intermediate command exits non-zero — only the
      # LAST line decides the step's outcome. So `ggcoder test` failing was
      # silently swallowed by `gg-boss test` succeeding right after it, and the
      # Windows leg reported SUCCESS while 72 ggcoder tests were failing. Every
      # Windows bug this suite was supposed to catch shipped through that gap.
      # bash's `-e` (set by the runner) makes each line fail the step.
      - name: Build framework packages
        shell: bash
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-ai build
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-agent build
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-core build
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/ggcoder build

      # Bundle growth is informational; measured CLI startup remains blocking.
      # Reference sizes live in .github/ci/baseline/sizes.json.
      - name: Size report + startup gate
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # --only: a positional arg is ignored by the script, which then checks
          # every artifact — including the sidecar this job never builds (that
          # one is reported in the `app` job, which bundles it).
          node .github/ci/size-gate.mjs --only dist:ggcoder
          node .github/ci/startup-gate.mjs
          node .github/ci/sidecar-startup-gate.mjs

      # Lint and formatting are OS-independent, so one leg is enough.
      - name: Lint + format check
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          pnpm lint
          pnpm format:check
          # The on-demand Claude Code download must match the pinned Agent SDK.
          node .github/ci/claude-code-manifest.mjs --check

      - name: Typecheck
        shell: bash
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-ai check
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-agent check
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-core check
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/ggcoder check

      - name: Test framework packages
        shell: bash
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-ai test
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-agent test
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-core test

      # Motion's media regressions decode real clips on every OS. CI-only
      # provisioning is intentional; never skip these tests when a tool is absent.
      - name: Ensure FFmpeg and ffprobe for Motion media tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if ! command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v ffprobe >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            case "$RUNNER_OS" in
              Linux)
                sudo apt-get update
                sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ffmpeg
                ;;
              macOS) HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew install ffmpeg ;;
              Windows)
                # The Chocolatey community feed intermittently 504s; retry
                # with backoff, and still fail the step if every attempt fails.
                for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
                  if choco install ffmpeg --version=8.0.1 -y --no-progress; then
                    break
                  fi
                  if [ "$attempt" -eq 4 ]; then
                    echo "choco install ffmpeg failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
                    exit 1
                  fi
                  delay=$((attempt * 30))
                  echo "choco install ffmpeg failed (attempt $attempt); retrying in ${delay}s" >&2
                  sleep "$delay"
                done
                ;;
              *) echo "Unsupported media-test runner: $RUNNER_OS" >&2; exit 1 ;;
            esac
          fi
          ffmpeg -version
          ffprobe -version

      # Blocking on every OS, Windows included. This started as a 72-failure
      # Windows backlog that had been invisible because the default PowerShell
      # shell swallowed it (see above); it is now zero, so the leg is a real
      # gate again. Do NOT reintroduce continue-on-error to get a red build
      # green — a non-blocking Windows leg is how the original bugs shipped.
      - name: Test ggcoder
        shell: bash
        run: pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/ggcoder test

  # Distribution-critical cross-OS job: stages the per-platform Node runtime,
  # bundles the sidecar, boots it with the bundled runtime (smoke), and runs the
  # Rust unit tests that gate path/window-chrome resolution. The full
  # `tauri build` lives in release.yml; this keeps CI fast while still
  # exercising the per-OS spawn path that breaks installed bundles.
  app:
    name: app · ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # 30 not 15: the Windows and Linux legs compile the Tauri tree and
    # build/launch an MSI or .deb (~12 min warm; much slower cold-cache).
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # pnpm version comes from package.json's packageManager field.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22.x
          cache: pnpm

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt

      # Both `cargo test` and the Windows packaged build compile the same large
      # Tauri dependency tree; without a cache the packaged smoke would rebuild
      # it from scratch on every run.
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: gg-app/src-tauri

      - name: Linux system deps (tauri)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf libayatana-appindicator3-dev

      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # shell: bash for the same reason as the `test` job — on Windows a
      # PowerShell multi-line step only reports the LAST line's exit code, so a
      # failing build here would pass silently.
      - name: Build framework packages
        shell: bash
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-ai build
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-agent build
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/gg-core build
          pnpm --filter @kenkaiiii/ggcoder build

      - name: Stage node runtime + bundle sidecar
        run: |
          pnpm --filter gg-app stage:node
          pnpm --filter gg-app bundle:sidecar
        shell: bash

      - name: Sidecar smoke (bundled runtime + bundle, per-OS)
        run: node gg-app/scripts/smoke-sidecar.mjs
        shell: bash

      # OS-independent slice of the sidecar bundle (app-sidecar.mjs + skills;
      # node_modules carries platform-conditional binaries so one baseline
      # cannot hold across the matrix).
      - name: Sidecar size report
        run: node .github/ci/size-gate.mjs --only sidecar
        shell: bash

      - name: Frontend build + initial JavaScript size report
        shell: bash
        run: |
          pnpm --filter gg-app build
          node .github/ci/size-gate.mjs --only frontend:initial

      - name: Frontend platform-class test
        run: pnpm --filter gg-app test

      - name: Rust format check
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        working-directory: gg-app/src-tauri
        shell: bash
        run: cargo fmt --check

      # Every OS: lib.rs has Windows- and macOS-only code paths.
      - name: Rust lint (clippy)
        working-directory: gg-app/src-tauri
        shell: bash
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Rust unit tests (path + window-chrome resolution)
        working-directory: gg-app/src-tauri
        run: cargo test

      # Windows-only, and the ONLY job that exercises real installer output.
      # `smoke-sidecar` above proves the bundled runtime loads, but it launches
      # the sidecar directly — it cannot catch what actually breaks for a
      # Windows user who installed the app: the shell failing to find
      # `ggnode.exe` beside the exe, the sidecar resource missing from the MSI,
      # or the app starting with no visible window. This builds an MSI,
      # administratively extracts it (installs nothing), launches it with a
      # throwaway user profile, and requires a visible window plus a packaged
      # ggnode child running the packaged bundle.
      #
      # The macOS leg skips the release build; it runs in parallel and stays fast.
      - name: Packaged app smoke (MSI build + launch)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        working-directory: gg-app
        run: pnpm smoke:packaged

      # Linux twin of the step above: builds a .deb, unpacks it with
      # `dpkg-deb -x` (installs nothing), launches it on a virtual X display
      # with a throwaway profile, and requires a visible window plus the
      # packaged ggnode child running the packaged bundle.
      - name: Packaged app smoke (deb build + launch, Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        working-directory: gg-app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends xvfb xdotool dbus
          xvfb-run -a dbus-run-session -- pnpm smoke:packaged:linux

repository.readme:
# World Monitor [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](README.ja-JP.md) | [Русский](README.ru.md) **Real-time global intelligence dashboard** — AI-powered news aggregation, geopolitical monitoring, and infrastructure tracking in a unified situational awareness interface. [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/koala73/worldmonitor?style=social)](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/stargazers) [![License: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL%20v3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0) [![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-007ACC?style=flat&logo=typescript&logoColor=white)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/koala73/worldmonitor)](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/commits/main) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/koala73/worldmonitor?style=flat)](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/releases/latest) [![npm: worldmonitor](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/worldmonitor?logo=npm&label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/worldmonitor) [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/koala73/worldmonitor)](https://skills.sh/koala73/worldmonitor)

         

       

     

Documentation  ·  Releases  ·  Contributing

![World Monitor Dashboard](docs/images/worldmonitor-7-mar-2026.jpg) ## Ways to Use It | Surface | Get it | Docs | |---------|--------|------| | **Web app** | [worldmonitor.app](https://www.worldmonitor.app) and the tech, finance, commodity, happy and energy variants | [Getting Started](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/getting-started) | | **Desktop app** (Tauri) | Windows, macOS and Linux downloads above | [Desktop App](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/desktop-app) | | **Terminal dashboard** | `npx worldmonitor` | [Terminal Dashboard](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli-dashboard) | | **CLI** | `npm install -g worldmonitor` or `brew install worldmonitor` | [Command-Line Client](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli) | | **SDKs** | Python `worldmonitor-sdk`, Ruby `worldmonitor`, Go `sdk/go` | [SDKs](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks) | | **MCP server** | `https://worldmonitor.app/mcp` | [MCP Overview](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/mcp-overview) | The terminal dashboard runs the same live data in your shell: world map, news, markets, conflict, military flights, cyber, climate, prediction markets and live TV, with mouse support and colour themes. No API key needed. ![World Monitor terminal dashboard](docs/images/tui/overview.webp) --- ## What It Does - **Curated news feeds** across global and regional categories, AI-synthesized into briefs - **Dual map engine** — 3D globe (globe.gl) and WebGL flat map (deck.gl) with a shared map-layer catalog - **Panel inventory** — concrete panel implementations across specialized variants - **Cross-stream correlation** — military, economic, disaster, and escalation signal convergence - **[Country Instability Index (CII)](https://www.worldmonitor.app/country-instability-index/)** — live CII v14 scores, bands, and approximate 24-hour movement for 31 Tier-1 countries - **Finance radar** — stock exchanges, commodities, crypto, and a market composite - **Local AI** — run everything with Ollama, no API keys required - **Site variants** from a single codebase (world, tech, finance, commodity, happy, energy) - **Native desktop app** (Tauri 2) for macOS, Windows, and Linux - **Multilingual UI** with native-language feeds and RTL support For the full feature list, architecture, data sources, and algorithms, see the **[documentation](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/documentation)**. --- ## Support Status All site variants and desktop binaries are built from a single codebase and ship from the same release process. The table below clarifies maintenance status so you know which surfaces are safe to depend on. | Surface | Status | Notes | |---------|--------|-------| | `worldmonitor.app`, `tech.`, `finance.`, `commodity.`, `happy.`, `energy.` | Stable | Public deployments built from this repo, actively maintained | | Desktop binaries (Windows / macOS Apple Silicon / macOS Intel / Linux AppImage x64 and ARM64) | Stable | One Tauri binary for every variant — install World Monitor and switch to tech, finance, commodity, energy, or happy in-app. There is deliberately no per-variant download | | `worldmonitor` npm package (terminal dashboard and CLI) | Stable | Published from [`cli/`](cli/) on every `cli-v*` tag | Issues filed against any of the above are triaged from the same backlog — see the [issues board](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/issues) for currently-open work. --- ## Quick Start Requires Node.js 24, the version pinned in `.nvmrc`. Distribution packages are often older. Debian 12 and Raspberry Pi OS ship Node.js 18 with npm 9.2.0, where `npm install` stops with `Invalid comparator: file:vendor/braces`. Install Node.js 24 with [nvm](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm) (`nvm install` inside the checkout reads `.nvmrc`) or from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/download). ```bash git clone https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor.git cd worldmonitor npm install npm run dev ``` Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) (override the port with `DEV_PORT` in `.env.local`). The app runs with no environment variables. Feature-specific data sources may require credentials. See `.env.example` for the full list. For variant-specific development: ```bash npm run dev:tech # tech.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:finance # finance.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:commodity # commodity.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:happy # happy.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:energy # energy.worldmonitor.app ``` See the **[self-hosting guide](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/getting-started)** for deployment options (Vercel, Docker, static). --- ## Tech Stack | Category | Technologies | |----------|-------------| | **Frontend** | Vanilla TypeScript, Vite, globe.gl + Three.js, deck.gl + MapLibre GL | | **Desktop** | Tauri 2 (Rust) with Node.js sidecar | | **AI/ML** | Ollama / OpenRouter, Transformers.js (browser-side) | | **API Contracts** | Protocol Buffers and sebuf HTTP annotations | | **Deployment** | Vercel Edge Functions, Railway relay, Tauri, PWA | | **Caching** | Redis (Upstash), 3-tier cache, CDN, service worker | Full stack details in the **[architecture docs](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/architecture)**. --- ## Programmatic Access World Monitor is built for agents and scripts as well as browsers: - **MCP server** — `https://worldmonitor.app/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). Public `tools/list`; `tools/call` authenticates with a `X-WorldMonitor-Key` header or OAuth. The server also publishes its Agent Skills through the draft `io.modelcontextprotocol/skills` extension (`skills/list`, `skills/get`, and `skill://…` resource reads). - **Google Antigravity and Gemini listing preparation** — install the bundled Antigravity plugin (`.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json` + `mcp_config.json`) with `agy plugin install ./worldmonitor`. Gemini custom apps and Connected Apps sign in through Google's OAuth callbacks. See [Gemini and Antigravity](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/gemini-antigravity). - **REST API** — base `https://api.worldmonitor.app`, described by the [OpenAPI spec](https://worldmonitor.app/openapi.yaml). - **CLI** — the official [`worldmonitor`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/worldmonitor) npm package (source in [`cli/`](cli/)). Run it with no arguments in a terminal for the [terminal dashboard](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli-dashboard): ```sh npx worldmonitor tools # run ad-hoc — list every MCP tool (no key needed) npm install -g worldmonitor # or install the `worldmonitor` (alias `wm`) command brew install worldmonitor # or install it with Homebrew worldmonitor risk IR --api-key wm_xxx ``` - **SDKs** — official zero-dependency client libraries mirroring the CLI: Python [`worldmonitor-sdk`](https://pypi.org/project/worldmonitor-sdk/) (source in [`sdk/python/`](sdk/python/)), Ruby [`worldmonitor`](https://rubygems.org/gems/worldmonitor) ([`sdk/ruby/`](sdk/ruby/)), Go [`github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/sdk/go`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/sdk/go) ([`sdk/go/`](sdk/go/)). Guide: [worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks). Agent discovery files: [`llms.txt`](https://worldmonitor.app/llms.txt) · [agent-skills manifest](https://worldmonitor.app/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json) · [api-catalog](https://worldmonitor.app/.well-known/api-catalog). Get an API key at [worldmonitor.app/pro](https://www.worldmonitor.app/pro). --- ## Flight Data Flight data provided graciously by [Wingbits](https://wingbits.com?utm_source=worldmonitor&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=worldmonitor), the most advanced ADS-B flight data solution. --- ## Supported By World Monitor's web app and API run on [Vercel](https://vercel.com?utm_source=worldmonitor&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=worldmonitor). Thank you to Vercel for their generous support of the project. --- ## Data Sources WorldMonitor aggregates attributed upstream sources across geopolitics, finance, energy, climate, aviation, cyber, military, infrastructure, and news intelligence. Curated feeds and freshness-tracked source groups are published in the full [data sources catalog](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/data-sources), with provider, feed-tier, license-posture, and collection-method details. --- ## Contributing Contributions welcome! See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines. ```bash npm run typecheck # Type checking npm run build:full # Production build ``` --- ## License **AGPL-3.0-only** for the source code. Commercial use is permitted under the AGPL when you comply with its copyleft and source-availability terms. | Use Case | Allowed? | |----------|----------| | Personal / research / educational | Yes, under AGPL-3.0-only | | Self-hosted instance | Yes, under AGPL-3.0-only | | Fork and modify | Yes, share source under AGPL-3.0-only when required | | Commercial use / SaaS | Yes, under AGPL-3.0-only when you comply with AGPL obligations | | Private-source proprietary use or official branding rights | Separate commercial or trademark permission needed | See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for the full code license and [docs/license.mdx](docs/license.mdx) for a plain-language summary. Commercial licensing is available as an alternative option for teams that need non-AGPL terms. Copyright (C) 2024-2026 Elie Habib. All rights reserved. --- ## Author **Elie Habib** — [GitHub](https://github.com/koala73) ## Contributors ## Security Acknowledgments We thank the following researchers for responsibly disclosing security issues: - **Cody Richard** — Disclosed three security findings covering IPC command exposure, renderer-to-sidecar trust boundary analysis, and fetch patch credential injection architecture (2026) See our [Security Policy](./SECURITY.md) for responsible disclosure guidelines. ---

name: Test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# A superseded PR run owes nobody a verdict. Branch protection and
# deploy-gate.sh both evaluate the head SHA only. Letting it finish burned
# 59% of this workflow's runs on dead commits and queued the live commit
# behind them. Cancellation is pull_request-only. A push to main still owes
# the deploy gate a verdict, and `github.run_id` gives it a group of one so
# nothing can evict it (#8443).
concurrency:
  group: test-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      code: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.code }}
      browser: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.browser }}
      digest: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.digest }}
      validation: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.validation }}
      umami: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.umami }}
      consumer_prices: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.consumer_prices }}
      desktop_config: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.desktop_config }}
      desktop_rust: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.desktop_rust }}
      zapier: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.zapier }}
      durations_key: ${{ steps.durations.outputs.cache-matched-key }}
    steps:
      # The newest shard duration estimates CI has measured, found once per run
      # so every unit shard partitions the inventory from the same file: each
      # shard computes the whole partition and keeps its part, so two shards
      # reading different estimates would drop or repeat test files. The shards
      # save new entries as they finish. A PR run finds its own newest entry or
      # main's. No entry, or a failed lookup, leaves the key empty and every
      # shard falls back to scripts/shared/data-test-durations.json.
      - name: Find the newest measured test durations
        id: durations
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/data-test-durations/durations.json
          # A key nothing is saved under: actions/cache prefix-matches the
          # primary key before restore-keys, so a run_id here would make a
          # re-run of an old run prefer its own stale entry over the newest.
          key: data-test-durations-v1-lookup
          restore-keys: data-test-durations-v1-
          lookup-only: true
      - id: diff
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # Specialized jobs (desktop-rust, umami, digest, …) are path-filtered
          # on PRs. Do the same on push to main. Forcing them true here used to
          # compile the Tauri crate and rebuild Umami images on every merge —
          # weather, news, embed — which is not a desktop or analytics gate.
          # Fail open (run everything) only when we cannot see the file list:
          # a zero parent SHA, a compare error, or GitHub's 300-file cap.
          emit_all_true() {
            echo "browser=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "code=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "digest=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "validation=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "umami=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "consumer_prices=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "desktop_config=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "desktop_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "zapier=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          }
          ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "push" ]; then
            BEFORE="${{ github.event.before }}"
            if [ -z "$BEFORE" ] || [ "$BEFORE" = "$ZERO" ]; then
              echo "No usable parent SHA; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
            if ! COMPARE_JSON=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/compare/${BEFORE}...${{ github.sha }}"); then
              echo "Compare API failed; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
            if ! FILES_JSON=$(jq -ce '.files | arrays' <<< "$COMPARE_JSON"); then
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
            FILE_COUNT=$(jq 'length' <<< "$FILES_JSON")
            if [ "$FILE_COUNT" -ge 300 ]; then
              echo "Compare listing is truncated at 300 files; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            if ! PR_JSON=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${{ github.event.number }}") ||
               ! FILES_JSON=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${{ github.event.number }}/files" --paginate --slurp | jq -ce 'add | arrays'); then
              echo "PR file lookup failed; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
            FILE_COUNT=$(jq 'length' <<< "$FILES_JSON")
            if ! jq -e --arg head "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" \
              --arg base "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}" --argjson count "$FILE_COUNT" \
              '.head.sha == $head and .base.sha == $base and .changed_files == $count and $count < 3000' <<< "$PR_JSON" >/dev/null; then
              echo "PR metadata moved or its file list is incomplete; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Include both sides of renames. A deleted file is still an input.
          # Refuse line-delimiter characters before passing paths to awk.
          if [ "$FILE_COUNT" -eq 0 ] || ! FILES=$(jq -er '
            [.[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)]
            | if all(.[]; type == "string" and length > 0 and (explode | all(. != 0 and . != 10 and . != 13)))
              then .[] else error("invalid path listing") end
          ' <<< "$FILES_JSON"); then
            echo "Unusable file list; running every Test job."
            emit_all_true
            exit 0
          fi
          CODE=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^docs\/research\/seo-ai-visibility\// { count++; next }
            # Committed resilience acceptance artifacts are docs-path data that
            # tests/dry-run-resilience-education-flip.test.mts validates —
            # recomputing gates, checking provenance, and rejecting a
            # self-declared verdict. That validator lives in the `unit` job, so
            # without this rule the guard skips on exactly the PR that commits
            # an artifact and can only ever fire on unrelated changes.
            /^docs\/snapshots\/resilience-.*-acceptance-.*\.json$/ { count++; next }
            # Per-service OpenAPI specs are generated machine artifacts consumed
            # by tests/openapi-filter-param-schemas.test.mjs, which enumerates
            # every JSON spec. Keep the JSON/YAML siblings on the same `unit`
            # job when a PR changes only docs/api output (#6650).
            /^docs\/api\/[^\/]+Service\.openapi\.(json|yaml)$/ { count++; next }
            # The generated OpenAPI bundle sits under docs/ but is the INPUT to
            # the served public/openapi.json. Its <= 950,000-byte scanner guard
            # (tests/openapi-json-dedup.test.mjs) and the capacity report that
            # tracks the approach to it both run in `unit`, so without this
            # carve-out a PR that only regenerates the bundle sets code=false
            # and skips the one gate that measures the artifact it changed
            # (#6558).
            /^docs\/api\/worldmonitor\.openapi\.yaml$/ { count++; next }
            # The Data Coverage block in public/ai-search.md is generated from
            # the inventory registries, and the docs-stats volatile-claim gate
            # exempts that block precisely because
            # tests/ai-search-product-facts.test.mjs fails when it drifts from
            # the generator. That test lives in the `unit` job, so without this
            # rule the only gate on a fabricated figure skips on exactly the PR
            # that edits the file (#6038). NOTE: no apostrophes in this awk
            # program - it is single-quoted in the shell, so one would end it.
            /^public\/ai-search\.md$/ { count++; next }
            # A published ranking snapshot is the source of the ranked-country
            # figure and captured date in public/ai-search.md. A snapshot-only
            # PR would otherwise set code=false, skip the byte test, and land a
            # snapshot whose figures the committed page no longer matches -
            # surfacing later as a confusing failure on an unrelated PR.
            /^docs\/snapshots\/resilience-ranking-[0-9-]+\.json$/ { count++; next }
            /^blog-site\/src\/content\/blog\/.*\.md$/ { count++; next }
            /^blog-site\/src\/content\/guides\/.*\.md$/ { count++; next }
            # public/home.md is the agent-mode homepage and the residue guard
            # asserts it links the comparison hub (#7746). Without this rule a
            # home.md-only PR sets code=false and that guard never runs.
            /^public\/home\.md$/ { count++; next }
            /\.md$/ { next }
            /^docs\// { next }
            # A src-tauri node suite is run by sidecar and policed by
            # tests/package-test-command-paths.test.mjs inside unit; both are
            # gated on code, so the exclusion below must not swallow it (#7772).
            /^src-tauri\/.*\.test\.(mjs|mts|cjs|js|ts|tsx)$/ { count++; next }
            /^src-tauri\// && $0 !~ /^src-tauri\/sidecar\// && $0 !~ /^src-tauri\/.*\.json$/ { next }
            /^CHANGELOG\.md$/ { next }
            /^LICENSE$/ { next }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/docker-publish\.yml$/ { next }
            { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "code=$( [ "$CODE" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          ZAPIER=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^integrations\/zapier\// { count++; next }
            /^shared\/event-triggers\.json$/ { count++; next }
            /^tests\/package-test-command-paths\.test\.mjs$/ { count++; next }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/test\.yml$/ { count++; next }
            /^\.github\/scripts\/deploy-gate\.sh$/ { count++; next }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "zapier=$( [ "$ZAPIER" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Only proven non-browser inputs may skip this job. New paths run it
          # until their owner can establish that they cannot affect the smoke.
          BROWSER=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^(src\/|api\/|server\/|shared\/|public\/|pro-test\/|e2e\/)/ { count++; next }
            /^docs\// { next }
            /^tests\/.*\.test\.(mjs|mts)$/ { next }
            /^scripts\/(audit-railway-watch-paths|run-railway-registry-sync|railway-services)\.(mjs|json)$/ { next }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/(railway-registry-sync|seed-freshness)\.yml$/ { next }
            /^\.husky\// { next }
            /\.md$/ || /^LICENSE$/ { next }
            /^src-tauri\// { next }
            { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "browser=$( [ "$BROWSER" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # digest-image job: build Dockerfile.digest-notifications when a PR
          # touches its inputs (scripts/, shared/, server/_shared/, api/, the
          # Dockerfile itself, or the root package manifest). Catches the
          # cross-directory-import + native-dep breakage class documented in
          # tests/dockerfile-digest-notifications-imports.test.mjs.
          DIGEST=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^(scripts\/|shared\/|server\/_shared\/|api\/|\.dockerignore$|Dockerfile\.digest-notifications|package\.json|package-lock\.json)/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "digest=$( [ "$DIGEST" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # resilience-validation-smoke job: run the no-secrets artifact/schema
          # and script-contract gate when the validation bundle, its Dockerfile,
          # its committed artifacts, or its focused tests change.
          VALIDATION=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^Dockerfile\.seed-bundle-resilience-validation$/ { count++ }
            /^docs\/methodology\/country-resilience-index\/validation\// { count++ }
            /^package\.json$/ || /^package-lock\.json$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/benchmark-resilience-external\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/backtest-resilience-outcomes\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/validate-resilience-sensitivity\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/seed-bundle-resilience-validation\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/_bundle-runner\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^tests\/(resilience-validation-artifacts-schema|benchmark-resilience-external|backtest-resilience-outcomes|resilience-sensitivity-v2|seed-bundle-resilience-validation)\.test\.(mjs|mts)$/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "validation=$( [ "$VALIDATION" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Umami's database race cannot be covered by the normal no-Docker
          # unit suite. Run a real PostgreSQL gate only when its managed image,
          # migration, patch, or focused tests change. Do not trigger on every
          # Test workflow edit: unit already pins the job shape, and rebuilding
          # two Umami images is the cost that made this look like a per-PR tax.
          UMAMI=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^\.dockerignore$/ { count++ }
            /^Dockerfile\.umami$/ { count++ }
            /^Dockerfile\.umami-retention$/ { count++ }
            /^docker\/umami\// { count++ }
            /^scripts\/umami-retention\.sql$/ { count++ }
            /^tests\/umami-(runtime-remediation\.test|postgres-integration|runtime-write-probe)\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "umami=$( [ "$UMAMI" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Consumer-prices-core has its own lockfile and Vitest suite, so run
          # it whenever package code, tests, or its CI definition changes.
          CONSUMER_PRICES=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^consumer-prices-core\// { count++ }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/test\.yml$/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "consumer_prices=$( [ "$CONSUMER_PRICES" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Desktop drift gates (#5902). The `code` filter above deliberately
          # skips src-tauri/ (non-sidecar), so before these outputs existed a
          # Rust/Tauri-config change ran zero PR CI and desktop breakage
          # surfaced only at the next release build — months later.
          # Any `src-tauri/**/*.json` is carved back into `code`:
          # tests/desktop-one-binary-model.test.mjs asserts on the set of Tauri
          # bundle configs (#5908) and runs in `unit`. Without the carve-out,
          # adding a per-variant config would skip its own gate — and the
          # carve-out covers every JSON path, not just `tauri*.conf.json`, so a
          # config parked at e.g. `src-tauri/profiles/commodity.json` cannot
          # sneak past it either.
          # The sidecar handler bundle build lives in the `unit` job (gated on
          # `code`), NOT here: the bundled api/{domain}/v1/[rpc].ts handlers
          # import from src/ and server/ via the @/ alias, so the bundle's
          # real input graph is the whole code surface, and `code` is the
          # filter that already tracks it.
          DESKTOP_CONFIG=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^src-tauri\// { count++; next }
            /^package\.json$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/repack-linux-appimage\.sh$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/check-desktop-build-env\.mjs$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/sync-desktop-version\.mjs$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/check-rust-security-floors\.mjs$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/download-node\.sh$/ { count++; next }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/.*\.ya?ml$/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "desktop_config=$( [ "$DESKTOP_CONFIG" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Compile the Tauri crate only when the crate itself changes.
          # Workflow edits are covered by desktop-config (cheap) and by the
          # unit contract that pins this job's shape — they must not pay
          # cargo test --locked (45 min budget) the way test.yml used to.
          DESKTOP_RUST=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^src-tauri\/sidecar\// { next }
            /^src-tauri\// { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "desktop_rust=$( [ "$DESKTOP_RUST" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  zapier:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.zapier == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: integrations/zapier
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: integrations/zapier/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
      - run: npm test

  docs-stats:
    # Always-on: derives build-owned inventory facts and validates fixed or
    # semantic documentation contracts. Runs on every PR/push (docs-only PRs
    # set changes.code=false and skip `unit`, so this must not gate on it).
    # Docs date generation uses the existing YAML parser for OpenAPI pages.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          # Docs page dates derive from git history; a shallow checkout would
          # resolve every file to HEAD instead of its last content change.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - uses: ./.github/actions/install-root-deps
      - name: Generate and validate build-owned inventory facts
        run: |
          node scripts/generate-inventory-facts.mjs
          node scripts/generate-inventory-facts.mjs --check
      - name: Doc claims match code
        run: node scripts/docs-stats.mjs --check
      - name: Generate and validate docs page dates for this revision
        run: |
          node scripts/generate-docs-page-dates.mjs
          node scripts/generate-docs-page-dates.mjs --check
          node --test tests/docs-page-dates.test.mjs
      - name: Every English docs page has a zh translation
        # Docs-only PRs skip the unit shards, so without this step a missing
        # docs/zh mirror surfaces only as a red main after merge (#8968).
        run: node --test tests/docs-i18n-parity.test.mjs
      - name: Published internal links resolve without redirects
        run: node --import tsx --test tests/internal-link-redirects.test.mjs
      - name: Derived files are current (npm run generate)
        # Every committed generated file with a freshness check: product facts,
        # llms.txt, AI search, source attribution, the homepage teaser strip,
        # the entitlement crosswalk (exit 2 there means a missing source, and
        # its output is printed), catalogs and notices. Always-on because a
        # docs-only PR skips `unit`, yet docs feed several of these. zh-TW is
        # skipped here (no OpenCC) and checked in unit-built-output.
        run: node scripts/generate-derived.mjs --check

  unit-shards:
    name: unit-shard (${{ matrix.shard }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Three shards, not two (#7805): after #7769 split the browser job,
        # unit-shard (2) became the Test wall at 5m45s, of which ~2 min is
        # setup and builds every shard repeated and ~3 min is test:data. The
        # builds now run once in unit-built-output. Four, not three: the
        # test:data step saturates the runner's CPU, so a fourth runner is the
        # cheapest way to get more parallelism. Three paired benchmark runs took
        # the slowest shard from 236-269s to 176-186s. Five, not four: after
        # the other Test jobs got faster the unit shards (~207s) were the
        # slowest job again; on the same runner image the slowest test:data
        # step took 123s at five shards and 138-155s at four (bench run
        # 40083951067), and raising concurrency to 6 or 8 did not help. The
        # sharder balances by measured durations and is generic in the count,
        # so the denominator on the test:data step below is the only other
        # place this number lives. tests/ci-test-selection.test.mjs pins that
        # denominator to this matrix's length, and tests/data-test-shards.test.mjs
        # reads the matrix and proves the shards together run the inventory
        # exactly once.
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          # Suites such as crawlable-corpus and docs-page-dates read commit
          # history (last-modified dates, base drift), so the graph stays
          # complete. Blobless: file contents outside the checked-out tree are
          # fetched only if a suite asks for one, which cuts the clone ~3x.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      # tests/pizzint-history-redis.test.mjs is the only place the PizzINT
      # archive's Lua runs against a real server: the relay harness stubs the
      # EVAL and the proxy command-gate test only matches the script TEXT. That
      # suite self-skips when the binaries are absent, so without this step the
      # capacity refusal, newest-capture-wins compare, EXPIREAT and atomic
      # seed-meta update were verified by nothing in CI. ubuntu-latest does not
      # ship redis-server, so every shard installs it. The action installs
      # from a package cache with dpkg (a slow mirror used to put 24-58s on
      # the slowest shard), refreshes the stale index only on a miss, and
      # fails the shard if the binaries are missing.
      #
      # It runs before install-root-deps, not beside it: both composite actions
      # use actions/cache, and when a job does not reference it at the top
      # level, a parallel group made the runner download it twice at once and
      # one copy failed ("Could not find file .../actions/cache/<sha>/examples.md",
      # run 39936254975). This job now references actions/cache/restore and
      # save directly, so the runner fetches them at setup; keep the steps
      # sequential anyway.
      - name: Install Redis for the archive Lua suite
        uses: ./.github/actions/install-redis
      - uses: ./.github/actions/install-root-deps
      # The two nested trees are restored whole, like the root tree. Restoring
      # setup-node's npm download cache for them cost 4-9s per shard, and the
      # two installs another 7-10s. The key hashes every file that decides
      # their contents; bump the version when an install command below (or
      # ci:blog-site in package.json) changes.
      - name: Restore blog-site and scripts/ dependencies
        id: nested-deps
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: |
            blog-site/node_modules
            scripts/node_modules
          key: nested-deps-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-node24-${{ hashFiles('blog-site/package.json', 'blog-site/package-lock.json', 'blog-site/.npmrc', 'scripts/package.json', 'scripts/package-lock.json', 'scripts/.npmrc', '.npmrc', 'vendor/http-cache-semantics/**') }}
      - name: Install blog-site deps for SEO contract tests
        # Unit-only nested install; keeps postinstall free of blog-site.
        # tests/dependency-backports.test.mjs checks the patched source Astro
        # installs, and skips that check when blog-site/node_modules is absent.
        if: steps.nested-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm run ci:blog-site
      - name: Install scripts/ deps for the seeder link check
        # Railway seeders install scripts/package-lock.json, not the root tree.
        # tests/nixpacks-seeder-import-graph.test.mjs links their named package
        # imports against this install (#9608 shipped an undici 8 import to an
        # undici 7 container with every suite green). WM_EXPECT_SCRIPTS_DEPS
        # below fails the shard if a restored tree is missing it.
        if: steps.nested-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm ci --prefix scripts --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
      - name: Save blog-site and scripts/ dependencies
        if: steps.nested-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: |
            blog-site/node_modules
            scripts/node_modules
          key: ${{ steps.nested-deps.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      # The exact entry the changes job found, with no fallback key: a shard
      # that read anything else would partition differently from the others,
      # so a miss fails the shard instead.
      - name: Restore the newest measured durations
        if: needs.changes.outputs.durations_key != ''
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/data-test-durations/durations.json
          key: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.durations_key }}
          fail-on-cache-miss: true
      - name: Data tests without built output
        # No build here: the unit-built-output job builds dist/ and public/pro/
        # once and runs every suite that names them. The marker stays set, so a
        # guarded suite that lands in a shard fails instead of skipping.
        env:
          WM_EXPECT_BUILT_OUTPUT: '1'
          WM_EXPECT_SCRIPTS_DEPS: '1'
          DURATIONS_KEY: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.durations_key }}
        run: npm run test:data -- --built-output=exclude --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/5 --concurrency=4 --timings=${{ runner.temp }}/data-test-timings.jsonl ${DURATIONS_KEY:+--durations="$HOME/data-test-durations/durations.json"}
      # The next run's estimates, saved whether the tests passed or not: a cache
      # saved only by green runs goes stale exactly while main is red. The next
      # run reads only the newest entry, so if every shard saved, whichever
      # finished last would win and the same shard could win every run. One
      # shard saves per run instead: the one after the shard that saved the
      # entry this run restored (the key ends in its number), so the turn
      # rotates within each cache scope, a PR's or main's. It moves its own
      # files halfway to what they measured; if its tests failed it saves the
      # estimates unchanged, so a red shard passes the turn on instead of
      # holding it. Neither step can fail the shard.
      - name: Blend this shard's timings into the estimates
        id: blend-durations
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          DURATIONS_KEY: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.durations_key }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
          SHARD_TOTAL: ${{ strategy.job-total }}
        run: |
          last=0
          [[ "$DURATIONS_KEY" =~ -([0-9]+)$ ]] && last=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
          saver=$(( last % SHARD_TOTAL + 1 ))
          if (( saver != SHARD )); then
            echo "Shard $saver saves this run's estimates, not this one."
            exit 0
          fi
          previous=scripts/shared/data-test-durations.json
          [ -n "$DURATIONS_KEY" ] && previous="$HOME/data-test-durations/durations.json"
          next="$RUNNER_TEMP/next-durations.json"
          node scripts/refresh-data-test-durations.mjs --blend --previous "$previous" --output "$next" "$RUNNER_TEMP/data-test-timings.jsonl" || true
          [ -f "$next" ] || cp "$previous" "$next"
          mkdir -p "$HOME/data-test-durations"
          mv "$next" "$HOME/data-test-durations/durations.json"
          echo "updated=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Save the estimates for the next run
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.blend-durations.outputs.updated == 'true' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/data-test-durations/durations.json
          key: data-test-durations-v1-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-${{ matrix.shard }}
      - name: Upload data test timings
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6
        with:
          name: data-test-timings-${{ matrix.shard }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/data-test-timings.jsonl
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

  # Everything the shards would otherwise repeat three times: the /pro and
  # dashboard builds, the bundle budgets that read them, the suites that need
  # built output (scripts/run-data-tests.mjs --built-output=only), and the
  # tree-wide checks that do not depend on a shard.
  unit-built-output:
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          # The health-probe cutover gate compares the exact PR base with the
          # candidate tree. A shallow checkout would make that gate vacuous.
          # Blobless like the unit shards: the gate reads one blob
          # (api/health.js at the base), fetched on demand.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - uses: ./.github/actions/install-root-deps
      # Like the unit shards' nested-deps cache: the two nested trees are
      # restored whole. Before, setup-node restored the npm download cache for
      # all three lockfiles (6-9s, most of it the root's), and the two installs
      # still took 3s (blog-site) and 12s (pro-test). The key hashes every
      # file that decides their contents (both trees link packages from
      # vendor/); bump the version when an install command below, ci:blog-site,
      # or the install half of build:pro in package.json changes.
      - name: Restore blog-site and pro-test dependencies
        id: built-output-deps
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: |
            blog-site/node_modules
            pro-test/node_modules
          key: built-output-deps-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-node24-${{ hashFiles('blog-site/package.json', 'blog-site/package-lock.json', 'blog-site/.npmrc', 'pro-test/package.json', 'pro-test/package-lock.json', 'pro-test/.npmrc', '.npmrc', 'vendor/**') }}
      - name: Install blog-site deps
        if: steps.built-output-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm run ci:blog-site
      - name: Install /pro deps
        # The install half of build:pro; the build step below runs the other.
        if: steps.built-output-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        env:
          npm_config_allow_scripts: ''
        run: npm --prefix pro-test ci --prefer-offline
      - name: Save blog-site and pro-test dependencies
        if: steps.built-output-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: |
            blog-site/node_modules
            pro-test/node_modules
          key: ${{ steps.built-output-deps.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: zh-TW catalogues reproduce from their Simplified source (#6555)
        # The zh-TW catalogues are generated from zh.json, not translated from
        # en.json, so the EN baseline in translate-locales.mjs is the wrong
        # instrument for them and reports them separately. That leaves this as
        # the only check that fails when zh.json moves and nobody reran the
        # generator — without it, key-existence stays green while the values
